Chaudhary — India-born but having arrived on a tourist visa six years ago, staying due to COVID travel restrictions — was named player of the match; his parents had flown from India for their first game watching him play in Australia. The two sides are scheduled to contest the second T20I on Tuesday at Carrara on the Gold Coast south of Brisbane.
items.title: Nikhil Chaudhary's all-round display powers Australia past England in T20I thriller at MCG

items.summary: After a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile and two other objects—believed to be another missile and a jet-powered drone—struck Polish territory on Friday, NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said Saturday that all allies stand in full solidarity with Poland. The incident occurred while the Coalition of the Willing was conducting military exercises nearby; per TVP reporting, authorities were still assessing circumstances as Rutte called the breach dangerous and unacceptable. Speaking to TVP Info after talks with Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in Warsaw, Rutte said the response by Polish F-16 fighter jets backed by NATO exemplified how the alliance should work. The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War assessed that Russia timed the incursions to coincide with the drills to test NATO's response and deter support for Ukraine, noting that Polish officials requested additional NATO forces and air defense capabilities—though Warsaw did not invoke Article 4 consultations. These details are drawn from unverified reporting by TVP and assessments attributed to ISW rather than confirmed facts.
items.title: NATO chief says allies stand with Poland after Russian airspace breach

items.summary: Cricket leg-spinner Yuzvendra Chahal made his political debut on Saturday by joining the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and being named a 'Special Invitee' to the party's newly formed National OBC Morcha executive committee. The BJP announced these appointments as per directions from national president Nitin Nabin, effective immediately; Maurya said they followed instructions from that same source. Chahal will represent Delhi in the wing dedicated to Other Backward Classes, a move expected to strengthen the BJP ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections where OBC voters form a significant bloc. On X on [d1: November 21, 2026], he thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin, and OBC Morcha national president Amarpal Maurya for the inclusion. The announcement also named seven national vice presidents (Jogen Mohan from Assam, Mamata Mohanta from Odisha, Sangam Lal Gupta from Uttar Pradesh, Babanrao Raoji Chaudhary from Maharashtra, Sat Prakash Rana from Delhi, Arjun Sahni from Bihar, and Sangeeta Balwant Bind from Uttar Pradesh), three national general secretaries (Gajendra Yadav from Delhi, Pramod Madhwaraj from Karnataka, and Lalit Chandrakar from Chhattisgarh), seven additional national secretaries, and 37 members of the national executive committee. Born in [d2: 1990], Chahal is described as the first Indian bowler to take [q2: 400 wickets] in T20 cricket, with best figures of 6/25 against England; Punjab bought him for Rs [q3: 18 crore ahead] of the [d3: 2025] season. He has played county cricket in England and represents Haryana domestically.
items.title: Yuzvendra Chahal joins BJP as OBC Morcha 'Special Invitee'

items.summary: A viral video circulating on X after the August 2026 APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, purportedly shows Russian President Vladimir Putin extending his hand for a handshake that Chinese President Xi Jinping turns away from, prompting speculation about diplomatic tensions between Beijing and Moscow. The footage is fake: FRANCE 24 traced it via reverse image search to authentic material filmed during the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation meeting in Kyrgyzstan in August [d1: 2026], where both leaders clearly shake hands with no indication of a snub, and falsely presented as recent APEC summit footage when original video from that gathering also shows them shaking hands. The creator's post has accumulated more than [q4: 10 million views] and was flagged as AI-generated content; the account describes itself as satire and openly acknowledged producing the clip with Grok Imagine, an AI tool developed by Elon Musk's xAI.
items.title: Viral AI-Generated Video Depicts Xi Jinping 'Snubbing' Putin at APEC Summit; FRANCE 24 Confirms Footage Is Fake and Misattributed to Recent Meeting

items.summary: The BADBOX malware botnet has returned following last year's disruptions, generating a record 40 billion fraudulent advertising bid requests per day through infected Android-based devices. According to HUMAN's Satori researchers, who uncovered and disrupted the latest variant, BADBOX 3.0 had grown into the largest documented ad-fraud operation by daily bid request volume. At its height, BADBOX 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform. Its volume was more than three times that of VASTFLUX, the previous record holder, and represents a larger peak than the last five years' worth of published Satori investigations combined.
items.title: BADBOX botnet returns with record-breaking daily ad fraud volume

items.summary: According to a report by JM Financial, around seven sectors recorded high levels of mutual-fund selling in October, each exceeding Rs [q1: 2,500 million] in total outflows. Cement led with the highest selling at Rs [q4: 8,004 million], followed closely by Hotels, Restaurants & Tourism at Rs [q7: 7,544 million]. Private Banks saw a total of Rs [q10: 7,310 million] in selling. Coal recorded Rs [q13: 6,915 million], PSU Banks Rs [q16: 4,919 million], Port & Logistics Rs [q19: 3,502 million], and Insurance Rs [q22: 2,586 million]. The report lists the top five stocks sold and top three bought within each sector. These figures are drawn from a single JM Financial report covering only October's mutual-fund flows across these seven sectors; they do not include other months or all market sectors.
items.title: Seven sectors saw heavy mutual-fund selling in October 2026

items.summary: Instagram has introduced a feature allowing users to edit Stories after publishing them, according to Instagram chief Adam Mosseri. The update lets users correct text, change music, adjust stickers, and modify drawings without re-uploading the content. A key benefit is that editing preserves existing engagement—views, likes, and replies—whereas previously correcting an error required deleting the Story and posting a replacement, which erased accumulated interactions; Mosseri noted this was among the most requested improvements. The feature is accessed via the three-dot menu at the bottom-right of an open Story, where users select 'Edit Story,' after which the post displays an 'Edited' label to viewers. However, editing is restricted to a 15-minute window following publication; once it closes, the option becomes unavailable. Separately, Instagram announced additional creative tools including stickers with more fonts, colors, and shapes, a redesigned sticker selector, improved multi-photo selection and layout options, plus blur effects and gradient backgrounds for better image fitting within Story frames. The article presents these details as reported by Mosseri without independent verification of the feature's rollout status or broader user adoption.
items.title: Instagram Adds Post-Publishing Story Editing With 15-Minute Window

items.summary: Researchers from Columbia University and CertiK introduced TensorLean, a Lean-based framework that formally verifies GPU kernels at the PTX level by proving compiled kernel code matches tensor-level mathematical specifications. The system starts from unmodified source code; developers write specs in Lean built on Mathlib with five components (spec_math, spec_mut, spec_layout, spec_tol, and requires), after which TensorLean checks four properties—no data races, termination, correct output within tolerance, and untouched memory elsewhere—through a seven-step pipeline that compiles to PTX, builds happens-before graphs for race detection, symbolically executes code across schedules, lowers specs to the PTX-memory level, and discharges proofs using Lean's kernel along with Z3 and cvc5. Scaling techniques include reducing concurrency problems to sequential ones via symbolic coverage of all CTAs, threads, and loop iterations; semiring-based loop invariants for tiled accumulating loops like online softmax requiring one SMT query per loop; algebraic error proofing at zero combined with separately bounded round-off errors; and assertions added as hints that are proved once then reused. The team evaluated 149 kernel instances spanning FlashAttention-2, -3, and -4 plus DeepGEMM (and other projects), proving 83 correct while uncovering 38 bugs across six projects—of which 23 were in FlashAttention variants—and reported that it caught a data race in FlashAttention-4 absent from 17,760 test runs. Of the 102 FlashAttention instances examined, 56 passed all four properties while the other 46 each failed on an identified source bug. The framework reportedly runs on a 16-core workstation and checks PTX compiled for A100, H100, and B200 kernels; its specs total about 10,278 lines against roughly 151,285 lines of kernel source (a near-15:1 ratio), with a stated 1.8K-line PTX parser. The authors note the main gap versus Volta is configuration coverage, since equivalence checkers unroll loops for one concrete setup at a time while TensorLean uses symbolic parameters; however, these claims are self-reported by the team and should be treated as vendor assertions rather than independently verified findings.
items.title: Columbia and CertiK Researchers Introduce TensorLean for Formal Verification of GPU Kernels

items.summary:
The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC), an independent agency established by Congress in 2000, released its latest annual report asserting that China's support for Pakistan during Operation Sindoor complicated Indian operational planning and tied down Indian military resources. The commission argues this aligns with Beijing's broader objective of constraining India as a peer competitor in the Indo-Pacific region.

The USCC states that May 2025 demonstrated how China could strengthen Pakistan during a crisis without directly entering the conflict, making two-front contingency planning an increasingly critical concern for India. The report further claims India's dependence on Chinese manufacturing has become leverage for Beijing and a vulnerability for the United States, citing examples where China restricted industrial inputs to India, required Indian firms to certify that Chinese-supplied goods would not be reexported to the US, and used pricing strategies to undercut new Indian pharmaceutical production.

The commission also asserts that China's expanding naval and surveillance presence is eroding India's strategic advantages in the Indian Ocean, with Beijing reportedly bringing its South China Sea approach to the region by renaming undersea features. The report frames these developments as complicating US efforts to diversify supply chains away from China toward India.

The claims originate solely from the USCC annual report and represent that agency's assessment; no independent verification of these assertions is provided in the source text.
items.title: US-China Economic and Security Review Commission Report Attributes Complications in India's Military Planning to China-Pakistan Support During Operation Sindoor

items.summary: Mexican special forces arrested Fausto Isidro "Chapo" Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation (Guasave Cartel) and a member of the FBI's 10 most wanted list, on Friday in Guasave, Sinaloa. The detention followed an operation using US intelligence to locate him; forces established a perimeter before coming under gunfire and explosives during their entry into his property. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, along with four Mexican army members who had been travelling to reinforce security in the area. Eight people total were detained—Meza Flores plus seven others including his second-in-command (his cousin) and financial operator (his brother-in-law)—with Meza Flores, his cousin, and his brother-in-law flown to Mexico City for prosecution while five remained in Sinaloa. Authorities seized multiple weapons, including a grenade launcher, as well as drugs and cash.
items.title: Fausto Isidro 'Chapo' Meza Flores Arrested in Shootout in Guasave, Sinaloa

items.summary: On Saturday, cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and was appointed a special invitee to the national executive of its OBC morcha. This appointment came as part of a broader round of selections for party positions; BJP national president Nitin Nabin announced seven new national vice presidents for the OBC Morcha, representing Assam, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh (two), Maharashtra, Delhi, and Bihar. The text also includes an author bio describing Rohitashwa Ranjan as a digital journalist with The Times of India who frames Indian politics as staged production rather than reporting any additional details about Chahal's appointment or the morcha itself.
items.title: Cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal Joins BJP and Is Appointed to OBC Morcha Executive Committee

items.summary: Experts warn that Victoria's electricity supply is at risk when the Yallourn coal plant, which has operated since the 1970s and supplied about one-fifth of the state's energy, shuts down before 2028, with neither major party offering a clear plan to address the resulting shortfall ahead of this month's election. The challenge is compounded by rising demand from datacentres and electrification of buildings, homes and vehicles, which Oliver Nunn of Endgame Analytics says has driven electricity demand up about 5% year-on-year. Tim Baxter of Naru Research notes that cheap offshore gas from Bass Strait is declining with no evidence of meaningful replacement resources elsewhere, contributing to a reported 62% rise in gas prices over five years and an 18% increase in electricity bills; he argues that accelerating the build-out of windfarms, solar farms and batteries before 2028 reduces reliance on expensive gas. The Coalition under Liberal leader Jess Wilson is favoured to win but would scrap VNI West and pause the Western Renewables Link for a review, open doors to gas exploration, reverse Labor's all-electric homes policy, and tender firming capacity via an Energy Security Requirement modelled on NSW and South Australia schemes; it has not changed its 75%-80% below-2005-emissions target by 2035 or net zero by 2045. Labor would continue expanding the grid, shifting homes from gas to electricity, and supporting offshore windfarms while reviewing the Western Renewables Link; it has overseen renewable energy share rising from 10% to 44%, with windfarms growing from 14 to 44 and large-scale solar farms from two to 57 over Labor's 12 years in government, though both transmission links remain behind schedule per the auditor general. Analysts caution that whichever party wins, Victoria faces an energy shortfall without a viable plan.
items.title: Victoria's Electricity Supply Faces Shortfall as Yallourn Closes in 2028 Without a Clear Replacement Plan

items.summary: Australia's Wallabies ended a four-match losing streak with a 29-26 victory over Wales in Cardiff on Saturday, Nov. 22, securing their first European win in two years and advancing to a fifth-place Nations Championship playoff against Ireland at Twickenham on Friday. Coach Les Kiss attributed the result primarily to defensive improvement, noting that his restructured pack held up Wales over the line twice in the first half as defence stepped up throughout the match. Despite shipping 153 points across their four straight losses and conceding four Welsh tries after they entered the game buoyed by a prior All Blacks win, Kiss praised the team's three-to-four weeks of preparation and described it as a close contest that Wales won on energy. He credited smarter tactical play, including better aerial kicking management and more accurate decision-making, while acknowledging remaining concerns about discipline lapses that kept Wales in the match and yielded field position.
items.title: Wallabies coach Les Kiss credits defensive improvement after 29-26 win over Wales

items.summary: Manchester City extended an alarming losing run on Saturday, drawing 1-1 against Fulham and reaching what the source describes as a 'club in crisis.' The team that began the season with seven straight Premier League victories now sits four games without a win. Supporting figures cited include three defeats in its last four league matches—equal to the number of losses suffered across its previous 36 games—and nine consecutive games without a clean sheet across all competitions. The source frames these statistics as evidence of decline but offers no analysis of underlying causes, tactical adjustments, or any stated plans for recovery.
items.title: Manchester City's Slump Continues with Draw Against Fulham

items.summary:
Fred Nile, an ordained Congregational Union minister who served in the New South Wales Legislative Council for more than 40 years—entering the upper house in 1981 and retiring after unsuccessfully contesting the 2023 election—died peacefully on November 21 at age 92. His family announced his passing, noting he is survived by his wife, children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, with memorial details to be shared later.

Nile was a longstanding figurehead of the rightwing Christian Democratic party, which he led for decades, and served as an early standard-bearer for Christian and social conservative politics. The party and Nile frequently took positions opposing drug use, abortion, and homosexuality. Alex Greenwich, the member for Sydney, described their good working relationship despite political disagreement, particularly over protecting First Nations cultural sites, and credited Nile with playing a key role in passing legislation to expunge prior homosexual convictions that cleared hundreds of gay men.

Lyle Shelton, who had initially been chosen by Nile as his successor to lead the party in 2021 before their relationship soured, characterized Nile as someone who publicly championed Christian ethics and moral virtues at a time when few would. Greenwich reported having asked premier Chris Minns for a state funeral for Nile.
items.title: Rev Fred Nile, former NSW MP and Christian Democratic Party figurehead, dies aged 92

items.summary: Kelly, described as a fluffy long-haired orange-and-white cat approximately ten years old, is currently being fostered in Tokyo and visits the ARK office daily while seeking a permanent home. According to the source material, he exhibits sociable behavior by warming to newcomers within roughly 10 seconds through leg-rubbing, vocalization, head-bumping, and full-body stretches on the floor. The text states his preferred play activities include pussy-willow teaser toys and fetch, that he enjoys being brushed for fur maintenance, and characterizes him as friendly toward people, dogs, and cats. All behavioral descriptions are attributed to the source's promotional framing rather than independently verified observations.
items.title: Orange-and-white cat named Kelly seeks adoption

items.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice charged fourteen individuals in southern California with burglarizing more than $22 million worth of goods from moving freight trains, according to court documents and an indictment. The scheme, dubbed "Los Trenes," spanned 2024 through 2026 and involved raiding at least 36 trains while selling thousands of stolen Nike sneakers and other products on the black market. Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, is alleged to be the ringleader; court documents did not list an attorney for him or the others charged. The indictment details a consistent method: associates stowed away on moving freight trains with some serving as lookouts while others slashed the train's air hose to force an emergency stop, then loaded and concealed stolen goods at houses across southern California. Prosecutors characterized the theft scale as "staggering," per first assistant U.S. attorney Bill Essayli, and described the case as a 14-month investigation led by Los Angeles County district attorney Nathan Hochman, who said they aim to protect the supply chain from diversion to the black market. The heists reportedly continued even after law enforcement appeared to catch on; encrypted messaging between co-conspirators referenced arrests of buyers receiving stolen property in April and January 2026, yet the crew proceeded with further robberies through summer 2026. If convicted, the men face at least five years for conspiracy, up to 10 years for theft of interstate railroad cargo, or life imprisonment if violence against a railroad carrier is proven.
items.title: Fourteen people accused of a $22m freight-train burglary ring in southern California

items.summary: A boat carrying passengers between communities for a burial ceremony capsized on Friday in Bayelsa State within Nigeria's South-South region. According to National Emergency Management Agency spokesman Manzo Ezeki, at least 24 people have died and search-and-rescue operations are ongoing, though the number of missing persons has not been specified. Police spokesman Musa Mohammed reported that another 24 survivors were rescued and received medical care; however, authorities have not disclosed how many passengers were aboard when it sank. In response to the incident, Bayelsa Commissioner for Information Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai urged boat operators and passengers on Saturday to comply with safety regulations, specifically calling an end to overloading, speeding, recklessness, and travel without life jackets, noting that no journey is worth a life. The text frames this event within the broader pattern of recurring boat tragedies in Nigeria, attributing such incidents to inadequate enforcement of safety rules that permits faulty boats lacking life jackets to operate.
items.title: At Least 24 Dead After Boat Capsizes During Burial Ceremony in Bayelsa State, Nigeria

items.summary: Bloomberg News reported that the Trump administration is considering Sara Brenner, a senior Health and Human Services adviser, and Jeff Vacirca, head of a New York oncology group, as candidates to lead the Food and Drug Administration. A White House official stated that staffing decisions would be announced by the administration directly, dismissing any reporting before such an announcement as baseless speculation. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The claims originate from Bloomberg News, which was unable to be independently confirmed at the time of publication.
items.title: Trump Administration Considers Candidates for FDA Leadership Positions

items.summary:
The Victorian Greens obtained a court order preventing independent candidate Tosh-Jake Finnigan in the seat of Prahran from distributing how-to-vote cards that mimic the minor party's colours and font. The injunction was sought because these cards directed preferences away from the Greens, prompting legal action to stop their distribution.

In related political developments reported alongside this ruling, the Liberal Party announced that a coalition government would require Victoria's top prosecutor to face questions in parliament annually, while Labor announced funding for the Pat Cronin violence prevention foundation. These announcements are attributed to their respective parties and reflect separate policy positions rather than established outcomes.
items.title: Victorian Greens Win Court Injunction Against Prahran Independent Over How-to-Vote Cards

items.summary: On Saturday (Nov 21), Bahrain reported that an Iranian attack struck a civilian industrial facility, causing a fire but no injuries. The incident was part of the latest escalation in regional hostilities since the United States and Israel attacked Iran in February, during which Gulf Arab states have been drawn into repeated Iranian strikes across the region. Civil Defence teams worked to contain the fire at the site, though Bahrain's ministry provided no details on its location or nature; it gave only an alert urging residents to seek shelter before issuing an all-clear followed by a second alert. Separately, Bahrain's Defence Force said its air defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks, with shrapnel causing material damage but no casualties, and characterized Tehran as continuing a "systematic hostile approach." Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed their aerospace forces launched a combined missile-and-drone attack on US positions at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in retaliation for alleged aggression and repeated violations of Iranian airspace. The kingdom hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. US Central Command did not immediately respond to a request for comment, and Bahrain has reported intercepting multiple Iranian aerial attacks over recent days as Gulf states face continued fire from Tehran since the war began.
items.title: Iranian Missile-and-Drone Attack Hits Bahraini Industrial Facility as Air Defences Intercept Strikes on US Bases

items.summary: The starting grid for the third-to-last race of the 2026 Formula 1 season was set at the Las Vegas Strip with Max Verstappen taking pole position and Oscar Piastri dropping to 17th after a penalty. The text reports that Kimi Antonelli posted the fastest qualifying time, edging out Verstappen by 0.258 seconds in Q3's closing moments on a final lap completed just one second before its end; his recorded time was 1 minute, 33.893 seconds. However, Mercedes denied him an eighth pole of the season with a five-place grid penalty for exceeding engine allocation. Verstappen qualified ahead of George Russell (third) and Lando Norris (fourth), while Antonelli started third on the front row alongside Verstappen; both Ferraris missed Q3 for the first time since the 2025 Emilia-Romagna Grand Prix, with Charles Leclerc qualifying 11th and Lewis Hamilton 12th. Piastri qualified seventh but received a 10-place grid penalty because McLaren fitted him an upgraded internal combustion engine (ICE) exceeding his yearly allocation, while he and Norris used new turbochargers; the ICE was installed on his MCL40. Racing Bulls drivers Arvid Lindblad (sixth-fastest time) and Liam Lawson (eighth-fastest) both qualified in the top 10. The race is forecast to be roughly 10C at its start, which the text notes makes heating tyres difficult for all competitors.
items.title: F1 Las Vegas Grand Prix Grid Set: Verstappen on Pole, Piastri Penalized to 17th

items.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "El Chapo Isidro" and listed among the FBI's top 10 most-wanted fugitives, was captured by Mexican authorities overnight from Friday into Saturday with intelligence assistance from the Trump administration, according to Mexico's Secretary of Security and Citizen Protection, Omar Garcia Harfuch. The 44-year-old had a $5 million reward offered for information leading to his arrest. His detention immediately triggered violence in Sinaloa state that left at least 11 people dead; an overnight firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen killed seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers, per Mexico's Defence Cabinet, while terrorizing residents of Guasave with trucks and businesses set ablaze. Meza Flores rose from a scrap metal dealer to lead the Beltrán Leyva drug trafficking organization—which split from the Sinaloa Cartel in 2008—and later led his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization (also known as Los Mazatlecos), for over two decades. Authorities accuse him and his network of smuggling heroin, cocaine, fentanyl, methamphetamine, and marijuana into the United States, along with kidnapping, extortion, torture, and murder; he is also allied with "Los Mayos," a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the Trump administration. His capture comes more than 14 years after his first U.S. indictment and seven years after a federal superseding indictment was issued in the District of Columbia, charging him with multiple drug-trafficking violations plus firearm use and possession.
items.title: FBI's Most-Wanted Fugitive 'El Chapo Isidro' Captured in Mexico; Triggers Deadly Sinaloa Violence

items.summary: On 22 November, petrol and diesel prices held steady in 14 Indian cities including New Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. In New Delhi, petrol remained at ₹102.12 per litre and diesel at ₹95.20; Mumbai recorded petrol of ₹111.21 and diesel of ₹97.83. Among the four metros cited, Kolkata had the highest rates for both fuels—petrol at ₹113.51 and diesel at ₹99.82 per litre—with Chennai following at ₹107.76 petrol and ₹99.55 diesel. Hyderabad posted the nation's highest petrol rate among the 14 cities at ₹116.15, while Thiruvananthapuram recorded both its second-highest petrol price (₹115.49) and the highest diesel rate (₹104.40). Chandigarh had the lowest rates for both fuels among all 14 cities—petrol at ₹101.54 and diesel at ₹89.47—with Hyderabad's petrol exceeding Chandigarh's by ₹14.61 per litre, a gap that translated to an extra ₹146.10 on a 10-litre fill (₹1,161.50 in Hyderabad versus ₹1,015.40). The diesel spread between the highest and lowest cities was ₹14.93 per litre. Other reported rates included Noida petrol at ₹101.96 and diesel at ₹95.44; Lucknow petrol at ₹102.23 and diesel at ₹95.71; Gurgaon petrol at ₹102.97 and diesel at ₹95.64; Bengaluru petrol at ₹111.68 and diesel at ₹99.56; Bhubaneswar petrol at ₹108.97 and diesel above ₹100 (₹100.68); Jaipur petrol at ₹113.19 and diesel at ₹98.25; and Patna petrol at ₹113.35 and diesel at ₹99.36. CNG prices rose in several cities, with Hyderabad seeing the largest increase of ₹3 to ₹115 per kg—the highest rate—followed by Mumbai (₹2.50 rise to ₹91.50) and Mathura (₹2 rise to ₹104). Bengaluru, Bharatpur and Dewas each rose ₹1 to ₹99; Meerut and Sonipat reached ₹96.50 and ₹96 respectively; Firozabad rose 40 paise to ₹99.90; New Delhi and the NCR held at ₹86.98 with Mumbai ₹4.52 higher, while Chennai stayed at ₹99.50 and Rewari at ₹91.59. Hyderabad and Mathura were the only two locations with CNG above ₹100 per kg. All prices are sourced from Goodreturns.
items.title: Petrol, diesel prices unchanged across most Indian cities on 22 November; CNG rose in several locations

items.summary:
In Peru, two local governments granted native stingless bees legal personhood—the first insects in the world to receive such recognition—recognizing their rights to exist, reproduce, thrive, and maintain a healthy habitat, with authorized representatives permitted to bring conservation suits on their behalf when those interests are threatened. This reflects the broader legal concept of juristic persons: entities like companies that can own property, enter contracts, sue or be sued through representatives without being human. India has applied this idea previously; in 2019, the Punjab and Haryana High Court declared the entire animal kingdom a legal entity with corresponding rights and duties, directing citizens to act as guardians and establishing protections such as granting bullock carts right of way on roads.

The newsletter also examines why India lacks its own open-world blockbuster despite contributing heavily to global titles like GTA VI. Rockstar Games acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru's Dhruva Interactive—founded by Rajesh Rao in 1997—in 2019, and studios trained through EA, Ubisoft, and Zynga have since pursued original projects. The core obstacle is financial: India's gaming market leans on advertising because console/PC adoption remains nascent (most players use mobile) and getting users to make in-app purchases has been difficult; a 2021 PwC study found 74% of Indian gamers preferred watching ads over making in-game purchases. Premium PC or console games relying on in-game purchases may not generate meaningful revenue until long after release, unlike mobile titles that earn ad revenue quickly.

The text proposes alternatives without asserting them as proven: studios could target international premium audiences, partner with established publishers for funding and marketing, use subscriptions, or launch smaller playable versions to build community interest before attracting investment. It notes original IP ownership—not talent—appears to be the next hurdle. These recommendations are presented as possibilities rather than verified outcomes; all figures (the 2019 court ruling, Rockstar's acquisition date, PwC's 74% statistic) and plans are attributed to their stated sources within the newsletter.
items.title: Peru Grants Stingless Bees Legal Personhood; Newsletter Explores India's Open-World Game Gap

items.summary: Graham Dumpleton, who created mod_wsgi two decades ago and has long sought the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production, released Muru: an AI-assisted Rust server intended to provide tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python applications both during development and in production. He published a detailed account of the project as part of his development process, with 18 posts spanning from November 4 to November 21, 2026 covering topics including mod_wsgi's legacy, worker architecture, import-once/fork-many behavior, HTTPS in development, combining WSGI and ASGI, release-based updates rather than restarts, canaries without a service mesh, container tenant design, Kubernetes integration, scaling from reported metrics, scaling to zero, scheduled overlays, observability, an on-page toolbar, and tracing within that toolbar. Dumpleton emphasized that although AI may perform much of the surface-level work, deciding what is not yet good enough remains his responsibility, drawing on twenty years of experience with mod_wsgi; he stated his intention to continue polishing Muru until it becomes something both he and others would trust.
items.title: Graham Dumpleton publishes a detailed account of Muru, an AI-assisted Rust server for Python web apps

items.summary: The article argues that the National Capital Region's regional planning approach is flawed because it tries to manage environmental systems using shifting administrative boundaries rather than ecological ones. The NCR expanded from about 30,000 sq km in 1985 when Delhi's growth began spilling beyond its borders to roughly 55,000 sq km today, with authorities already discussing further boundary revisions; the region spans parts of Delhi plus districts in Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. The core problem is that environmental systems—air pollution, drainage, catchment areas, wetlands, forests and the Aravallis—do not respect administrative lines, creating two separate geographies: one of government jurisdiction and one of ecological reality. This gap is most visible in air quality management. The Commission for Air Quality Management was created by the Central government in 2021 because the airshed extends beyond state boundaries, giving it regional powers to issue directions across Delhi-NCR. In January, the commission reviewed implementation of Stage III and Stage IV Graded Response Action Plan measures—such as banning heavy goods vehicles, shutting non-essential industries, halting construction, and enforcing work-from-home or school closures—and found deficiencies ranging from 7% to 99.6% across mandated actions, with more than 50% of complaints unresolved in various categories and regions. The commission can issue directions and monitor compliance but cannot execute tasks like road sweeping, which raises dust, since those remain the responsibility of local municipalities; construction-site inspections depend on local authorities and pollution-control bodies; and waste management, traffic management and other measures still rely on existing administrative machinery. The author concludes that treating environmental problems as matters of regional governance without a well-thought-out implementation structure risks creating one commission per concern—potentially for water quality or the Aravallis—and possibly another to coordinate them all, instead of developing functional maps such as airshed, aquifer and drainage-catchment maps that reflect how interconnected systems actually operate.
items.title: Air quality commission's implementation findings expose limits of NCR's administrative governance

items.summary:
Indian cricketer Yuzvendra Chahal has become a special invitee to the Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) National OBC Morcha Executive Committee. According to reports, this development followed meetings with senior party leaders and represents another instance of notable sports personalities entering politics.

Chahal reportedly expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP National President Nitin Nabin, and OBC Morcha National President Amar Pal Maurya for the respect and position afforded within the party. The text attributes these statements to Chahal's reported remarks following his meetings with party officials.

The source material presents this event alongside unrelated items: a note that the monsoon session has remained unprorogued for 100 days amid opposition criticism, plus separate news about Donald Trump's comments on Iran and protests in Jammu and Kashmir over a recruitment exam cheating scandal. The text contains no stated limitations or caveats regarding Chahal's political affiliation beyond reporting it as an event.
items.title: Yuzvendra Chahal Joins BJP as Special Invitee to National OBC Morcha

items.summary: In Southern Lebanon, the Lebanese Army has begun taking over areas as Israeli forces withdraw following their departure. Amid this transition, one grieving family returned to their village and found nearly everything inside their house destroyed. The source material provides no further details about the family's identity, the specific cause or extent of the destruction beyond describing it as near-total, or information regarding any official response from Lebanese authorities. NPR issued a disclaimer clarifying that it does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews and that anyone making such requests is neither an NPR employee nor representing the organization.
items.title: Grieving Family Returns to Destroyed Village in Southern Lebanon After Israeli Withdrawal

items.summary: A framed lock of hair from former US President George Washington sold Saturday at auction through Richmond Auctions for $4,000 (£3,058); the new owner was not named. According to Richmond Auctions, the hair belonged to John Gadsby, a resident of what in 1799 was Alexandria, Virginia, who hosted Washington for dinner shortly before his death that same year and also entertained him at two birthday celebrations in 1798 and 1799. A testament given by Gadsby's granddaughter, Julia Ten Eyck McBlair, and posted on the Richmond Auctions website, states she obtained the hair from a descendant of Gadsby and had it framed to hang under Washington's portrait at her home in Washington City. The Saturday sale was not the most expensive for Washington hair: three strands thought to have been removed close to or after his death, stored in a locket, sold for nearly $40,000 in 2021. At least 50 locks of Washington's hair are preserved at Mount Vernon, his former residence and now museum; the site notes that public displays of hair peaked in the 19th century but had long been popular among affluent families like the Washingtons. Other associated items have also sold well: a signed 1776 letter from Washington asking for soldiers for the Continental Army sold in July for $109,800.
items.title: Framed Lock of George Washington's Hair Sells at Richmond Auctions for $4,000

items.summary:
The Lok Sabha's monsoon session has remained unprorogued for a record 100 days following adjournment sine die, prompting opposition parties to criticize the government over delays in convening the winter session. Opposition leaders allege that the government is attempting to increase its numbers to pass controversial delimitation laws, while the Congress party claims the delay reflects an effort to evade parliamentary scrutiny of demands for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and raises concerns about whether the winter session will be skipped in favor of a budget session. Regional parties have also raised objections regarding political maneuvering and called on the Lok Sabha Speaker for clarification.

The constitutional framework permits this arrangement: Article 85 empowers the President to prorogue either House, with provisions allowing a maximum six-month gap between sessions. The text notes that ongoing discussions include party positions and formulas related to seat increases.

Several limitations exist in attributing intent from these claims. Opposition allegations regarding motivations for delaying the winter session are presented as accusations rather than verified facts, and no independent confirmation of the government's stated reasons is provided within the source material.
items.title: India's Parliament Monsoon Session Remains Unprorogued for Record 100 Days Amid Opposition Criticism

items.summary: The article reports that Hyundai is planning to introduce a new electric version of its Porter work truck, which last received a model update 22 years ago. The current Porter remains in service across Korea and Southeast Asia as a cabover-style dropside pickup with box-like passenger cabs and professional-grade payload capacity. Spy shots published by Carscoops this month showed a heavily camouflaged prototype, reportedly following up on Kia's PV5 electric vans with a globally available EV version of the truck as early as next year. The design appears to replace Hyundai's conventional flat cabover with a short hood and crash structure, suggesting an attempt to meet Euro NCAP front-end protection standards rather than any confirmed safety certification. Beyond these visual details, no official specifications are stated; the article speculates that the vehicle may draw on the E-GMP.S commercial platform used by Kia PV vehicles, which offer 51.5 kWh and 71.2 kWh battery options paired with 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motors. The text poses an open question about whether a Western launch would use an AWD version of that platform or remain regional on a hybrid system, without providing any answer.
items.title: Hyundai reportedly preparing an all-electric Porter pickup, possibly on E-GMP.S platform

items.summary: At least nine people were killed and several others injured after a vehicle carrying pilgrims collided with a truck near Shambhupura on the Kota-Udaipur highway in Rajasthan's Kota district late Saturday night. According to Additional District Collector Rajesh Joshi speaking to ANI, the vehicle carried 16 people who all belonged to the same family; they were returning to Maharashtra after visiting Khatu Shyam when the accident occurred near Shambhupura around midnight. The administration reported that its immediate priority was ensuring injured passengers received proper medical care and recovery while post-mortem procedures began for those killed, with further details about the crash and the condition of survivors still awaited.
items.title: Nine Family Members Killed When Pilgrims' Vehicle Crashes Into Truck Near Shambhupura, Rajasthan

items.summary: In the first Test at Wellington's Basin Reserve on Sunday, India declared their innings at 720/9 on Day 4 to build a 352-run lead over New Zealand. The score set two records: it became the highest team total ever in a Test innings played in New Zealand, surpassing the hosts' previous best of 715/6 against Bangladesh in Hamilton in 2019; and it also broke the record for India's highest-ever Test total against New Zealand, edging out West Indies' 660/5 at this same ground in 1995. KL Rahul (136) and Rishabh Pant (128) led the batting while Glenn Phillips took 3/154 for New Zealand; India declared roughly an hour before tea with Dhruv Jurel dismissed last, after New Zealand had posted 368 in their first innings. The total was also notable as a rare feat: it marked only the second time any team has recorded six consecutive partnerships of at least 50 runs (Australia and Pakistan have done it once each), and India's top five batters all scored 80 or more, which had happened before only in Pakistan's innings against New Zealand in Abu Dhabi in 2014. The declaration made this India's fifth 700-plus Test total overall—placing them second on that list behind Sri Lanka (seven), ahead of England, Australia and West Indies (four each)—and their third-highest ever score, below 759/7 against England at Chennai in 2016 and 726/9 against Sri Lanka at Brabourne in 2009. The report offers no further context on match result beyond the stated lead.
items.title: India post highest-ever Test total in New Zealand with declaration at 720/9

items.summary:
A local court in Bengaluru issued an interim injunction on Saturday restraining Andhra Pradesh Congress Committee president Y S Sharmila, along with her family members, agents, and representatives, from interfering with the possession of a disputed bungalow at Yelahanka. The order was granted following a petition filed by Silicon Builders Private Ltd, which claimed to hold the property under a lease agreement executed on March 1, 2007, by E C Sugunamma—mother-in-law of YSR Congress party president Y S Jagan Mohan Reddy—for a term extending up to February 20, 2027. The company alleged that it had invested in maintaining agricultural activities, fruit-bearing trees, plants, irrigation facilities, guest houses, fencing, and other structures on the premises.

The dispute appears connected to Sharmila's decision to hold her daughter Y S Anjili Reddy's wedding at the palace on November 25, which Jagan reportedly objected to over security and privacy concerns. In a letter dated October 9, he conveyed his objections citing the influx of guests and event personnel into the residential premises; subsequently, Sharmila announced on October 31 that her family had shifted the wedding venue elsewhere while asserting full ownership of the property as part of a family partition.

The company's petition further claimed that registered gift deeds were executed on August 27, 2026, in favor of Sugunamma's daughter Y S Bharati Reddy and grandchildren, after which the lease was attorned to them. The plaintiff contended that Sharmila had attempted to interfere with its possession by sending third parties under the pretext of decoration work.

The court found that documents including the lease agreement, rent-payment records, electricity bills, and security-related materials prima facie supported the company's claim of peaceful possession as a lessee. It concluded that granting interim protection would not cause undue prejudice to Sharmila, who retains an opportunity to contest the application before December 19, when the case was posted for further hearing.
items.title: Bengaluru Court Restrains YS Sharmila from Entering Disputed Family Bungalow

items.summary: On November 22, Rishabh Pant scored his ninth Test century—128 off 153 balls at the Basin Reserve in Wellington—to become the first Asian wicketkeeper and only the sixth Indian batter to record a Test hundred in every SENA country (South Africa, England, New Zealand, Australia). His innings powered India to 629 for six at lunch on day four of their opening Test against New Zealand, extending their lead to 261 runs. With the knock, Pant joined an elite Indian group consisting of Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammad Azharuddin, Rahul Dravid, Virat Kohli, and KL Rahul who have all scored SENA-century totals; he is distinguished as the first wicketkeeper from Asia among them. His record-breaking run across these nations includes four centuries in England (114 at The Oval in 2018, 146 at Birmingham in 2022, and twin hundreds of 134 and 118 at Leeds in 2025), a 159 at Sydney in 2019, and an unbeaten 100 at Cape Town in 2022. The milestone followed Rahul's achievement the previous day as the fifth Indian batter and second Asian opener to score Test hundreds across all SENA countries. Pant also equalled Brendon McCullum's record for the second-highest number of sixes in a single Test innings, hitting 10 fours and six sixes, with his century reached via a reverse sweep off Glenn Phillips. The innings addressed earlier concerns about his fitness after he had been out of competitive cricket for seven weeks without clearance from the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru; his wicket-keeping and batting during the Test were cited as evidence that those doubts were resolved. Supporting India's dominance, Anshul Kamboj scored 38 off 42 balls earlier in the session, and Dhruv Jurel formed a rapid 75-run stand with Pant before being dismissed. Pant was eventually caught in the deep off Rachin Ravindra on the stroke of lunch.
items.title: Rishabh Pant becomes first Asian wicketkeeper to score Test centuries across all SENA nations

items.summary: A gender-based analysis of gold investment patterns in the UAE shows women owning gold at a substantially higher rate than men, with 76% of women compared to 58% of men. The data comes from the World Gold Council's report 'Gold Investment in the UAE: Consumer Insights and Market Opportunities,' which surveyed 2,000 respondents and found that 63% currently own gold in some form, making it the most widely held investment asset overall. While women lean toward physical gold ownership, men show relatively greater participation in cryptocurrencies and equities. The text does not state a specific survey date or margin of error.
items.title: Women Outpace Men in UAE Gold Ownership at 76% Versus 58%, Per World Gold Council Survey

items.summary:
West Bengal's Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has taken over an investigation into allegations that a man impersonated State Minister Kshudiram Tudu to influence the ongoing Staff Selection Commission (SSC) recruitment process. The accused, identified as Zulfiqar Ali of Deganga, was arrested by Bidhannagar Police following a written complaint submitted at Bidhannagar East Police Station by the SSC Secretary regarding WhatsApp messages allegedly sent to exert influence over the recruitment. CID Director General and IGP Natarajan Ramesh Babu confirmed that further details would be shared as the investigation proceeds.

The text notes this case is separate from an earlier September 15 incident in which Jharkhand's CID arrested two individuals—Sanjeet Kumar of Ranchi, who allegedly operated Shivangan Coaching Centre—for collecting money from candidates by promising to help them clear the 14th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) preliminary examination. The source presents these as alleged irregularities without confirming guilt or providing additional evidence beyond the reported arrests and complaints.
items.title: Man Arrested for Allegedly Impersonating Bengal Minister Kshudiram Tudu in SSC Recruitment Case

items.summary: Paolo Bulgari, grandson of Greek silversmith Sotirios Voulgaris and longtime head of the family jewellery business since the mid-1980s, has died in Rome at age 89. His family announced his death on Saturday, describing him as "the greatest jeweller of our time" while praising his humanity and entrepreneurial talent. Born in Rome in 1937, Bulgari joined the company shortly after leaving school to work alongside his father Giorgio, developing expertise in precious stones that shaped his later design and business career. Under his leadership with brothers Nicola and nephew Francesco Trapani, the brand shifted away from delicate Parisian aesthetics toward bold gemstones, rich yellow gold, generous proportions, and distinctive colour drawn from ancient Rome and Italian heritage, while expanding into New York, Paris, Geneva and Monte Carlo and diversifying into watches, perfumes, leather goods and hotels. In 2011 the family sold a controlling stake to French conglomerate LVMH in a deal valued at more than USD 5 billion, ending decades of direct family control. Bulgari also established the Paolo Bulgari Foundation in 2019 with his wife to support schooling and job training for young people in disadvantaged neighbourhoods on Rome's outskirts; he wrote that "at the origin of my surname there is a story of migration." His funeral is scheduled for Monday at the Basilica of Santa Croce in Rome.
items.title: Paolo Bulgari, architect of global luxury empire, dies at 89

items.summary: Xiaomi is selling its electric vehicles outside China for the first time ever, launching this week through local distributor Gargash Prime Automotive rather than operating its own retail network. The company's SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV are now listed for sale across the United Arab Emirates. Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun confirmed that Western car market entry would be announced at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on November 17, with official expansion into those markets scheduled for next year (2026). CarNewsChina reports Gargash Prime is offering 13 variants spanning the SU7 sedan, YU7 SUV, and Skynomad extended-range electric SUV lineup. Pricing starts at 169,900 AED (~$46,200) for the SU7 Standard and rises to 375,900 AED (~$102,000) for the range-topping SU7 Ultra. The SU7 Ultra is highlighted as a performance flagship with 1,548 hp from three electric motors, a sub-two-second 0-100 km/h time, and a 217 mph top speed. First customer deliveries of the SU7 Standard and Ultra, YU7 Standard, and Skynomad N70 Pro are scheduled for December (of this year), with remaining variants following in February 2027. The article notes these sales occur amid a broader wave of Chinese-built EVs entering Europe and Canada.
items.title: Xiaomi Begins Overseas EV Sales in UAE, Marking Its First Global Car Launch

items.summary: On Saturday, Bahrain accused Iran of striking a civilian industrial facility on Sitra Island—home to state oil company Bapco's refinery—causing a fire with no reported casualties. The interior ministry confirmed the attack without specifying its location, while residents described smoke rising over the island and Iran's Fars agency attributed strikes against two US bases there (Sheikh Isa and Juffair) to Revolutionary Guards action in response to alleged US actions. Simultaneously, UKMTO reported one tanker struck by an unknown projectile as it transited Hormuz with no casualties, while a second vessel was hit in its engine room; Iran later claimed the ship caught fire after entering a restricted zone and striking a mine—though US Central Command stated last month that mines had been cleared from main routes. These attacks ended a weeks-long lull following late-February US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which began an ongoing conflict over Hormuz, through which one-fifth of global oil flowed before the war; since summer, US forces have escorted ships and helped Gulf states export 1.5 billion barrels while maintaining its own counterblockade of Iranian ports. Diplomatically, deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran considers the US economic blockade an act of war it will lift through necessary measures, while Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called for talks to succeed and a rational lifting of the blockade—though Tehran insists on ending hostilities across all fronts, unfreezing assets, removing oil sanctions, and halting the counterblockade. Separately, Iran reported shooting down a US drone over Qeshm Island after American jets struck an Iranian missile site there Tuesday; President Masoud Pezeshkian warned that strikes on energy infrastructure would worsen winter power shortages, prompting his national electricity company head to announce rolling blackouts from Sunday due to fuel supply constraints. The summary reflects claims attributed to state media and officials without independent verification.
items.title: Bahrain Accuses Iran of Striking Industrial Site and Tankers in Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: The National Centre for Seismology (NCS) reported that a magnitude 4.1 earthquake struck Myanmar in the early hours of Sunday, November 22, 2026. According to an NCS post on X, the quake occurred at 2:35:57 AM Indian Standard Time, with its epicentre located at latitude 24.404 North and longitude 94.616 East in Myanmar, at a depth of 95 kilometres. The NCS provided these details as recorded values rather than an assessment of any impact or damage.
items.title: Myanmar Records 4.1 Magnitude Earthquake

items.summary: On Saturday, Iran launched two waves of drone and ballistic missile attacks on four US bases in Bahrain—home to the Fifth Fleet headquarters—with Fars news agency naming Sheikh Isa and Juffair among them. Iranian Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) claims stated that Patriot batteries and radar were hit, but neither Bahrain nor the US military confirmed these assertions; Bahrain instead reported intercepting several strikes and a civilian fire at an industrial compound with no injuries. Separately, explosions in Sirik, southern Iran, followed earlier US retaliation against Iranian facilities. In the Strait of Hormuz, at least three oil tankers were attacked Saturday: UKMTO said two tankers were struck separately by projectiles while exiting the Persian Gulf, and Iran's navy reported a tanker hit a mine east of the strait and caught fire—no casualties in any case. As these incidents rose over the past week, more than 14 Iranian tankers reportedly gathered off Kharg Island to break what Iran calls an illegal US blockade; deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi warned that breaching it could trigger a fierce response targeting Gulf energy infrastructure if engaged by the US military. Diplomatic activity continued in parallel: Qatar hosted talks with Iranian officials on Friday evening, and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi suggested reopening the Strait of Hormuz would be feasible if the US ended the blockade and lifted sanctions. President Trump separately said he sought a permanent deal to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons while ruling out regime change; however, the Institute for the Study of War noted that Iranian attempts to run the blockade create dilemmas for Washington—either collapse the blockade or risk war with unideal political costs—but no concrete outcome was stated.
items.title: Iran Strikes US Bases in Bahrain as Tankers Prepare to Break a Naval Blockade

items.summary: The article examines why people increasingly turn to absurd memes, sarcasm, and dark humour as an escape from stress caused by rising screen time and information overload. It presents six explanations: humour can make overwhelming situations feel less serious; relatable content about anxiety or burnout creates a sense of shared experience; dark humour lets people process difficult emotions through irony rather than direct confrontation; memes provide low-effort, instant entertainment compared to longer videos or articles; self-deprecating jokes reduce pressure around everyday imperfections and help with social fitting-in; and endless scrolling can paradoxically worsen the very screen fatigue it was meant to relieve. These points are attributed to specific sources: psychiatrist Dr Harish Shetty notes that dark humour may help people acknowledge uncomfortable feelings, while Gen Z content creator Amaan links the trend to dopamine-seeking behaviour and self-deprecating jokes as a way to avoid embarrassment. Raahi Doshi, a Gen Z graduate, cautions that using reels purely to suppress emotions can become unhealthy but remains acceptable for casual fun. The piece concludes with the caveat that memes offer only temporary relief rather than genuine rest or solutions, suggesting people should sometimes put their phones down instead of relying on digital content to manage stress.
items.title: Why Absurd Memes And Dark Humour Are Becoming A Popular Coping Mechanism

items.summary: On Saturday, Mexican forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores—known as 'El Chapo Isidro,' one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives—in Guasave, Sinaloa, after an overnight operation left seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers dead. The firefight erupted around 7 p.m. on Friday when armed forces came under attack with guns and explosives from suspected cartel operatives; authorities then established a security perimeter before entering the building where he was located to detain him. Because of intense resistance—including at least 10 roadblocks with burning vehicles—Mexican army and National Guard special forces could not extract Meza Flores until 4 a.m., after which eight people were detained total, including his No. 2. He was flown to Mexico City to appear before prosecutors. Meza Flores had led the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later headed his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization; he was also an ally of 'Los Mayos,' a Sinaloa Cartel faction designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the Trump administration last year. Mexico's government said intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture him but provided few details on how coordination occurred. The U.S. had offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest, and he was wanted for trafficking drugs into the United States and illegally carrying firearms. Following the capture, residents of Guasave—part of a 290,000-person municipality—reported widespread gunfire, burning cars and businesses, circling helicopters firing on people below, and thousands taking shelter in grocery stores; burned-out trucks blocked roadways leading into town. Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch posted that armed forces would remain deployed to protect civilians while lamenting the four soldiers killed. The DEA commended Mexican authorities as a security win, and U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said such results 'don't happen overnight' but are built on cooperation between partners. The capture is part of President Claudia Sheinbaum's more aggressive crackdown on cartels amid pressure from Trump; homicides have reportedly dipped significantly during her two years in office. However, experts warned the arrest could trigger further violence: security analyst David Saucedo said it reflects a longstanding 'kingpin strategy' that captures leaders without dismantling organizations—here, only Meza Flores and his No. 2 were taken while street-level dealers, businesses, and political and police connections reportedly remain intact—and noted such tactics often fuel violent power disputes among warring factions in the region.
items.title: Mexican authorities captured cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro' in a firefight that killed at least 11 people

items.summary: A recurring workplace anecdote—an anonymous Reddit commenter describing a boss who passively shames an employee for minimal engagement in group chats—raises the question of why Gen Z feels singled out. Career site Forage, written by a Gen Zer, notes that this generation is commonly labeled 'difficult' or 'hard to work with,' and cites a 2023 Resume Builder survey of 1,344 managers and business leaders in which 74% rated Gen Z harder to work with than other generations. However, the text treats this figure as measuring managerial perception rather than actual workplace performance, and flags that the company commissioned it. The Hindu frames generational labels as provisional stereotypes, questioning whether blamed traits are unique to Gen Z or simply reflect what any young generation experiences when taking on responsibility, while noting that older Indians' memories of hardship like ration-shop queues shape their views of work and entitlement. College counselor Kimberly Lobo attributes feeling targeted to overlapping forces—developmental age, greater exposure, social media, comparison, and environmental stress—and argues Gen Z is not simply more sensitive but grows up in a highly exposed, comparative environment while meeting normal developmental needs for identity formation; she rejects the 'fragile' characterization. Joe Moraes, 20, from Mumbai, describes criticism as landing equally online and offline because digital growth has blurred where identity lives, whereas his parents' generation received feedback privately. The text observes that generalization turns one person's thumbs-up into a verdict on all twenty-somethings, and quotes Geeta Giddi, whose 19-year-old son listens but ultimately does as he pleases—illustrating how the same behavior reads as disobedience to one generation and independence to another. The article concludes that feeling targeted may reflect constant observation, comparison, and judgment rather than oversensitivity.
items.title: Gen Z Feels Targeted at Work Despite No Evidence of Worse Performance

items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile struck President Volodymyr Zelensky's hometown in central Ukraine on Saturday, killing two people and wounding dozens. Hours after the attack, Zelensky reaffirmed his country's determination to join NATO.
items.title: Russia launches ballistic missile attack on central Ukraine

items.summary: Mexican special forces captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as "Chapo Isidro," during an operation in Sinaloa on Friday night. Footage released by Mexico's Defence Department shows heavily armed soldiers escorting the detainee into an army vehicle. Meza Flores was among the FBI's 10 most-wanted fugitives and is accused of trafficking drugs into the United States and illegally carrying firearms. Mexican authorities stated that intelligence provided by the Trump administration helped lead to his capture, though this claim originates from a source whose reliability should be independently verified rather than accepted at face value. Following the operation, violence erupted in the region, prompting security forces to remain deployed to protect civilians.
items.title: Mexico Captures FBI Most-Wanted Cartel Figure 'Chapo Isidro'

items.summary: A Russian cargo ship caught fire after being struck by drones on Saturday and subsequently drifted into Finnish waters, according to reporting from Kyiv. The vessel is affiliated with a major Russian military logistics company. Analysts cite a clear motive for the targeting; however, Ukrainian authorities have not confirmed or denied responsibility for the attack.
items.title: Russian Cargo Ship Set Ablaze by Drone Attack in Gulf of Finland

items.summary: Cameroon's under-17 team opened their FIFA U17 World Cup campaign in Doha with a 2-1 defeat to Venezuela, ending the match without securing its first points. Coach Thomas Libiih attributed the loss partly to lost momentum, stating that Cameroon missed some rhythm and did not deserve the result but slipped into it. Midfielder William Gueke described the team as slow to start in the first half before improving after halftime, framing the performance as a learning experience while reaffirming their goal of winning the tournament. Captain Krys Karel noted that Cameroon created chances but failed to convert them. The defeat leaves the squad seeking regrouping ahead of its next Group K match and focused on earning points to keep hopes of advancing to the round of 32 alive.
items.title: Cameroon U17s Lose World Cup Opener to Venezuela

items.summary: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a revised draft of the 2028 to 2034 EU budget, reducing it by €204 billion from an earlier European Commission proposal that drew criticism—especially from northern members including Germany—for being too large. The revision introduces new revenue channels intended to keep national contributions at a reasonable level; Costa described the plan as realistic and confident it provides a basis for agreement. The centerpiece is a tax on companies with annual digital-activity turnover of at least €50 million in the EU and €750 million worldwide, charging an annual contribution equal to 3% of net turnover from online advertising, digital intermediation services, and user-generated data. Other new own resources include taxes on tobacco products and electronic waste. Divisions persist: France called the draft 'deeply disappointing' and said it does not provide a basis for agreement because it falls short on Common Agricultural Policy income support for farmers.
items.title: European Council President Proposes Smaller EU Budget Funded in Part by a Big-Tech Tax

items.summary: A Russian ballistic missile double-tap strike on Friday evening hit Ukraine's southern city of Kryvyi Rih, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, killing two people — a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old woman — and wounding about 60 others, including several children, according to Ukrainian officials. City administration head Oleksandr Vilkul reported that the strikes caused fires and damage to roughly 25 apartment buildings, a hospital, schools, and an industrial facility via Telegram. Moscow separately confirmed another strike on Friday night in Kryvyi Rih, with Russia's Defense Ministry saying a thermal power plant was hit along with a power substation in Rivne; both facilities supply electricity to industry supporting Ukraine's military. The attacks came amid little progress in talks to end the nearly five-year-old war and after Ukraine struck the Kerch bridge linking Russian-occupied Crimea with Russia three times this week, prompting Putin to vow a "painful" response over what Moscow views as vital supplies for its southern forces. Beyond Kryvyi Rih, Russia reportedly struck a cargo vessel near Odesa carrying dual-use goods; an 11-person drone attack wounded people in Kharkiv including two children and one person was wounded in Kyiv; Ukrainian drones wounded three people in the Bryansk and Belgorod border regions of Russia; and Finland detected a Saturday morning drone attack on a Russian cargo ship in the eastern Baltic Sea, with Prime Minister Petteri Orpo warning that the war is "spilling over into our immediate vicinity." Zelenskyy warned NBC that the damaged Kerch bridge "will not remain standing anyway."
items.title: Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kryvyi Rih kill two and wound dozens

items.summary: Since taking office nearly two years ago, the Trump administration has expanded support for coal through executive orders and federal funding to keep aging plants open beyond their planned retirements. In September 2025, following passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act earlier that year, the Department of the Interior opened 13.1 million acres of federal land for coal leasing during a "Beautiful Clean Coal" event, with Secretary Doug Burgum citing reduced royalty rates and increased available acreage as economic and national security measures. An Environmental Defense Fund analysis of the 184 operating coal plants connected to the grid found that 90 receive financial, regulatory, or operational support from the administration — including $950 million in public funds distributed across 24 plants and Clean Air Act exemptions granted to 70 plants. EDF's Saruri Sarang characterized these measures as "cash handouts, free passes to pollute, and requirements to stay online past their retirement dates," arguing they raise electricity costs while increasing pollution for communities. The EPA's Mercury and Air Toxics Standards had reduced mercury emissions from coal- and oil-fired plants by more than 90 percent by 2026 after taking effect in 2015, with a further update in 2024; however, the administration permitted several firms to request exceptions on the basis of upgrade costs. The average U.S. coal plant is 44 years old and requires upgrades to operate effectively. Carbon emissions from the electric power sector rose 4 percent in 2025 relative to 2024 per the U.S. Energy Information Administration, with coal-fired electricity generation up 13 percent and raising coal-related CO2 emissions by 78 million metric tonnes. The article frames these figures as evidence that continued public financing of aging plants threatens human and environmental health while costing taxpayers billions rather than delivering cheaper power.
items.title: Trump Administration's Coal Support Costs Taxpayers Billions With Little Benefit

items.summary: Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said that, following trade agreements reached between UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European leaders in Brussels on Friday, the possibility of the UK rejoining the EU could be examined during informal discussions. The three announced deals covered food and drink standards, emissions trading, and a youth mobility scheme under which 100,000 young Britons would gain access to live, work, study, and travel in the EU with reciprocal rights for Europeans in the UK; Burnham estimated this agreement would add 0.5% to GDP, equivalent to £17bn. Miliband characterized these agreements as the limit achievable before the next general election, while noting that further brainstorming discussions with Brussels were planned over the following year and ahead of a UK-EU summit. However, the deals face potential disruption within six months if the EU blocks them unless European students pay domestic-level fees at British universities—a tuition-fee proposal reportedly not yet agreed—though Miliband insisted the food exports, energy, and youth mobility agreements would proceed regardless. The arrangements are scheduled to enter force in 2028 through legislation introduced next week. Labour has maintained its manifesto red lines since entering government in 2024, ruling out rejoining the single market or customs union and freedom of movement; Miliband affirmed these remain respected for this parliament while acknowledging that circumstances have changed materially since the 2016 vote. European Commission president Ursula von der Leyen expressed confidence a solution to the student-fee disagreement would be found.
items.title: UK Trade Agreements with EU Announced; Rejoining Bloc Kept as Open Option

items.summary: Despite gasoline prices falling nearly 60 cents in the past month, Americans traveling for Thanksgiving may still face higher pump costs than during any previous holiday. The national average dropped to $3.69 per gallon on Friday according to AAA, down from roughly $4.30 a year earlier, while GasBuddy projects an average of $3.62 on Thanksgiving Day—surpassing the prior record of $3.56 set in 2022. The decline reflects retreating crude oil prices and recovering supplies after disruptions tied to conflict involving Iran; West Texas Intermediate crude fell into the low $80s this week, U.S. gasoline inventories rose 5.1 million barrels to 215.9 million barrels, refineries switched to cheaper winter-blend fuel, and post-summer demand has softened. Travelers still pay about 60 cents more per gallon than last November, adding roughly $12 to a 500-mile round trip in a vehicle averaging 25 miles per gallon; AAA expects 72.9 million Americans to drive over the holiday versus 73.1 million the prior year, and GasBuddy reports nearly one in five drivers plans to cut other spending to cover fuel costs. Air travel offers little relief: AAA projects about 6 million flyers with domestic round-trip tickets averaging $800, up 17% from last Thanksgiving due to elevated jet fuel prices, while diesel averages around $5.90 per gallon and has pushed Thanksgiving dinner prices up 6%, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation. The outlook remains uncertain because Middle Eastern tanker traffic still faces attacks even as crude exports recover.
items.title: U.S. Gas Prices Could Hit a Thanksgiving Record Despite Month-Long Decline

items.summary: Rather than requiring separate apps, an expanding set of AI agents can be operated by texting them like ordinary people. These assistants reportedly remember context, connect to a user's existing email and calendar services, and complete tasks such as scheduling appointments, researching trips, sending emails, making reservations, shopping online, or setting reminders for later dates.
items.title: A growing roster of AI text-message agents competes for the personal-assistant space

items.summary: The 16th Biennale of Contemporary African Art opened in Dakar, Senegal, on Thursday under the theme "(Anti)fragility," which explores repair, resilience, and rebound as a way of transforming vulnerability into creative strength. The Democratic Republic of Congo is featured this year with its exhibition "Fourth Movement: Time as Living Matter." Curator Steve Bandoma describes the fourth movement as intangible, framing it as an encounter in front of a large mirror that prompts viewers to confront what has been done to people and Africa, examining the weight of history and each person's role. Ghanaian data artist Whitney Chinonye Ernest, part of a collective of women artists documenting the continent's journey toward democracy, says her participation lets her work reach hundreds or thousands of people and educate them about the effort behind African nations' milestones. Visitor Kuadio Adai noted it was his first time at the Biennale and described seeing the artwork as rewarding and powerful. Dak'Art 2026's official selection includes 54 artists from 17 African countries, with 22 in the Design section and three given carte blanche; around 450 projects are showcased across Dakar and other Senegalese cities until December 19.
items.title: Senegal's Dak'Art Biennale Opens Under Theme of (Anti)fragility

items.summary:
Shortical, a microdrama startup founded in January that produces short-form romantic series monetized primarily through subscriptions (typically the first 7–10 episodes are free before users pay to unlock full access), has begun pivoting toward AI-generated content because production costs for such material are substantially lower than live-action while profit potential is higher if an audience can be drawn. The company's latest microdrama, "Inevitable," premiered in Los Angeles and stars Aki Avni, a veteran Israeli actor with prior American television appearances including Fox's "24"; the project used his likeness to create a digital avatar playing himself in a meta plot about licensing one's face to a studio. This marked Shortical's first foray into likeness licensing, though CEO Guy Shimoni indicated it would likely not be its last.

In interviews with TechCrunch, Avni described the experience as both nerve-racking and exciting, framing AI as "a new kind of art" and himself as a pioneer in the format. Shimoni emphasized that AI enables smaller teams to produce movie-scale content—kingdoms, dragons, superheroes—that live-action budgets previously constrained. The company reported that while China has the largest microdrama audience globally, most of Shortical's viewers are U.S.-based; its demographic skews heavily female, with many watching at night for minor dopamine hits as they fall asleep, and several AI-generated titles reportedly have millions of views.

Shortical is now advertising a "LICENSE YOUR FACE" program on which interested parties submit social media handles to receive an offer setting out contract terms. A company representative stated this offering was still in its early days with no signed contracts yet, that the Avni series used a direct agreement rather than the platform process, and that Shortical hoped it would draw attention to face licensing before promoting the program more actively.

The trend has already taken hold in China, where microdrama originated.
