Overlapping wars and US President Donald Trump's foreign policy have further undermined multilateralism, which a negotiating process requiring consensus depends on — a requirement former Vice President Al Gore criticized as 'insane.' The draft decision included new calls for carbon capture seen by many teams as a cover for extending fossil fuel lifespans; it was supported by the Arab Group (including the UAE), China, India, and Japan, but adamantly opposed by least-developed-countries blocs as well as the UK and EU. Meanwhile, more than two dozen minor emitters adopted transition-away-from-fossil-fuels guidelines and nearly 90 countries pledged to accelerate electrification during COP31. The text notes that climate action became a casualty of energy turmoil rather than presenting this collapse as an inevitable outcome, and quotes Panama's former climate envoy Juan Carlos Monterrey Gómez asserting the green economy will win because it is cheaper and creates jobs rather than through negotiated texts — framing these smaller-group agreements as partial successes within a deeply fragmented process. The article presents the fragmentation as evidence of declining universal agreement on global energy pathways while acknowledging that real-world economic forces operate independently of UN-brokered summits, without establishing whether this collapse will ultimately prevent or merely delay broader climate action.
items.title: COP31 Climate Summit Collapsed Without Agreement

items.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) asked the civil aviation ministry to order an immediate financial and safety review of SpiceJet, warning that prolonged distress could undermine employee welfare, maintenance quality, operational reliability, and aviation safety. FIP president Captain C S Randhawa requested that the DGCA assess the airline's cash and working capital, outstanding salaries, statutory and airport dues, fuel payments, lessor liabilities, serviceable aircraft and crew levels, flight duty time compliance, engine support, critical spares, insurance, and the source, timing, and proposed use of a board-approved ₹5,500-crore fundraise. If SpiceJet could not demonstrate capacity to run its approved schedule safely, FIP argued its operations should be regulated in the interest of passenger safety. The federation attributed the crisis to weak working capital, lower fleet utilisation, continued fixed costs, accumulated dues, repeated reliance on fundraising, and rising dollar-denominated lease rentals as the rupee depreciated; it cited CARE Ratings for aviation turbine fuel accounting for about 36% of SpiceJet's overall costs in FY 2024-25. FIP warned that delayed salaries could cause financial anxiety, stress, fatigue, and reduced concentration among pilots and other safety-critical staff, while unpaid dues to lessors, airport operators, oil companies, maintenance providers, and vendors—some placed on cash-and-carry arrangements—had grounded a substantial part of the fleet and disrupted published schedules. FIP noted SpiceJet's domestic market share fell from about 21% in 2014 to nearly 0.6% in October 2026 amid persistent cash-flow problems, accumulated liabilities, and difficulty meeting daily financial commitments. The DGCA issued a show-cause notice on 17 November 2026 over operational disruptions, non-compliance, unpaid dues, grounded aircraft, and the absence of a credible recovery plan, giving SpiceJet seven days to respond. FIP stressed that although the ₹5,500-crore fundraise's timing and use are critical to revival, the problems appear systemic and cannot be resolved through short-term infusions alone; it urged that employee remuneration be treated as a priority operational obligation during financial stress and proposed mandatory annual health/safety-risk assessments for all scheduled airlines with quarterly monitoring for distressed carriers. The federation also called for lower, uniform VAT on aviation turbine fuel—potentially under the GST framework—and temporary relief or deferral of airport charges such as landing, parking, navigation, and ground-handling fees. These claims are drawn from FIP's letter to the civil aviation minister; figures like market share and cost percentages reflect reported estimates rather than independently verified data.
items.title: FIP Urges Government Intervention in SpiceJet Over Financial and Safety Concerns

items.summary: During his November 20-22 visit to New Delhi for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Civilisational Dialogue Forum, Pakistan's Climate Change Minister Musadik Masood Malik reported that he had not been invited for bilateral talks with Indian officials. Speaking in Delhi on November 22, Malik stated that any discussion of contentious issues would require a formal invitation and an established mechanism, noting that "without a mechanism" such discussions cannot occur. His visit was described as strictly multilateral; while he held bilateral meetings with Tajikistan and Iran representatives, no engagement took place with Indian counterparts. Malik indicated willingness to discuss specific topics if India initiated dialogue, including the Indus Waters Treaty, which he said had not been formally invited for discussion at that time. On terrorism, he argued discussions should be evidence-based rather than provocation-driven, claiming Pakistan had repeatedly offered bilateral or multilateral platforms for such talks. Separately, while Indian authorities approved Malik's request to visit security-cleared sites including the Taj Mahal in Agra and Humayun's Tomb in Delhi, his request to visit the Hazrat Nizamuddin Dargah was denied on security grounds according to India's Ministry of External Affairs.
items.title: Pakistan Climate Minister Says He Was Not Invited for Bilateral Talks With India

items.summary: United Nations climate negotiations held at COP31 in Antalya, Turkiye, failed on Sunday to produce an overarching agreement after several countries and the 27-nation European Union rejected a final proposal that made no explicit mention of fossil fuels. The talks ran nearly 48 hours overtime before collapsing without a main 'cover decision,' though negotiators noted progress had been made on smaller issues during the two-week session. Any pact at these negotiations requires near-unanimous consensus, and while Russia and Saudi Arabia pushed to keep fossil fuels out of the document, a larger number of nations accepted the deal—often reluctantly—prioritizing reaching some form of consensus over content they found insufficient. EU Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien condemned the outcome as 'unconscionable,' arguing it was unacceptable for a climate act to omit any reference to fossil fuels, which he identified as the chief cause of global warming. The impasse reflects a broader pattern: UN climate outcomes generally avoided explicitly naming fossil fuels during most of the first 25 years of negotiations until three years ago, when an agreement in the United Arab Emirates called for 'transitioning away from fossil fuels.' Since that Dubai deal, no explicit mention has appeared; the Turkish-Australian leadership proposal recalled it but did not satisfy many nations and environmental groups. The article notes that despite the failure on the cover decision, discussions continued afterward.
items.title: UN Climate Talks in Antalya Fail to Reach Fossil Fuel Agreement

items.summary: Australia's government aims to develop hydropower and Pumped Hydro Energy Storage (PHES) under its Powering Australia Plan, which targets 82 per cent renewable electricity by 2030 and net-zero emissions by 2050. The Australian Energy Market Operator expects storage demand to rise significantly as intermittent wind and solar power requires long-duration dispatchable storage; a draft 2026 Integrated System Plan estimates the country will need 27 GW of storage by 2030 and 55 GW by 2050. Australia currently operates around 8.5 GW of traditional and pumped hydropower across over 120 stations, providing between 5 per cent and 7 per cent of electricity, while an identified practical capacity exceeds 124 GW at potential project sites.
items.title: Snowy 2.0 Cost Balloons as Australia Pursues Hydropower Expansion

items.summary: In an ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 match on Sunday, India A captain Tilak Varma reached a fighting fifty off 95 deliveries with three boundaries against Pakistan A in a high-pressure chase of 314 runs. His knock came at a critical juncture when India A had slipped to 177/6 after 34.5 overs; the team's batting lineup otherwise struggled, as Abhishek Sharma had earlier provided an explosive start with 70 off 42 balls while others failed to build partnerships. With wickets falling at regular intervals and India A needing 137 runs from 91 deliveries remaining, Varma's presence was described as crucial for holding the innings together. At the time of reporting, Shahbaz Ahmed batted alongside him on 24 off 25 balls, with both players tasked with keeping India's hopes alive in the contest.
items.title: Tilak Varma Scores Fighting Fifty to Anchor India A Chase Against Pakistan A

items.summary: Oscar-winning composer AR Rahman revealed at a press conference during the International Film Festival of India on Sunday (November 22) that he spent nearly three years composing music for Nitesh Tiwari's two-part adaptation of Ramayana. During this period, he turned down approximately 10 to 12 film projects, including work with several prominent filmmakers, in order to remain focused on the project. Rahman composed alongside German composer Hans Zimmer and stated that some tracks underwent more than a dozen versions before finalization; specifically, 'Ravana Tandav' reportedly went through 12-13 iterations until the team settled on a version everyone liked. He expressed pride in his commitment while explaining that he only accepts projects he genuinely loves because they nourish his artistic sense and energize his team. Rahman also discussed balancing traditional Indian sounds with modern global influences, describing himself as multicultural and noting that combining these styles can be confusing but enjoyable to explore.
items.title: AR Rahman Dedicates Three Years to Ramayana Music, Turns Down 10-12 Films

items.summary:
E-commerce platform Cleverbridge disclosed that hackers breached its systems and stole customers' payment card information, including credit card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV/CVC security codes. The company detected unauthorized activity on November 4, 2026, temporarily took its systems offline to contain the breach, then brought all systems back online later that same day before determining a third party had copied stored payment card data. Cleverbridge began notifying affected customers on November 20, warning them of stolen payment details used for purchases through its platform.

While public disclosure confirmed theft without specifying which card details were compromised—referring customers to individual notifications—a breach notification shared with BleepingComputer revealed the stolen information included payment card numbers, expiration dates, and CVV/CVC codes. The notification explicitly stated that no other personal data (such as names, contact, or billing details) was copied, though it redacted the last four digits of affected cards.

The company has not disclosed how attackers gained access to its platform, how long they remained in systems, or how many customers were impacted—information BleepingComputer requested but Cleverbridge did not respond to. Of particular concern is the theft of CVV/CVC codes used to verify transactions. The incident was confirmed as not a ransomware attack, with no encrypted systems.

Cleverbridge notified data protection authorities, law enforcement, payment card networks, and payment partners about the breach. It engaged TransUnion's Cyberscout to distribute notifications and provide affected customers with complimentary credit monitoring and fraud assistance. Affected customers were advised to review statements for unauthorized transactions and contact their card issuers.

The text notes that Cleverbridge serves numerous technology brands including Red Hat, SUSE, Tenable, Veeam, Jamf, Sony, and Parallels, though it has not identified which of these businesses' customers were affected. The final section contains unrelated promotional content for Adaptive Security's email scanning service.
items.title: Cleverbridge Data Breach: Hackers Stole Credit Card Numbers and CVV Codes

items.summary: Saurav Das, co-convener of the Cockroach Janata Party, announced on Sunday that the party's flagship initiative, the Cockroach Club, would provide a physical space where young Indians could discuss politics and society, engage with intellectual traditions, read, watch films, attend cultural performances, question conventional thought, and relax. According to Das's explanatory post on X, the club aims to combine recreation with intellectual engagement so that visitors can learn and unwind in the same setting while developing their own perspectives about India's future. The announcement describes intended functions of the project but does not provide details such as a launch date, location, funding sources, or membership plans.
items.title: Cockroach Janata Party's Saurav Das Announces Cockroach Club Plan for India's Youth

items.summary: Delhi Traffic Police issued traffic advisories for Monday in connection with two events marking the Prakash Gurpurab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji: a VIP movement at Rajghat (Mahatma Gandhi's memorial) and a Nagar Kirtan procession organized by the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee. The police stated that restrictions would be enforced near Rajghat from 10 am to 11 am, contingent on VIP movement and traffic conditions, with diversions potentially imposed at ITO Chowk, Delhi Gate, Guru Nanak Chowk, Shantivan Chowk, Rajghat DTC Depot, and IP Flyover. Special arrangements were also announced for north Delhi from 3 pm onward, affecting BSZ Marg between ITO Chowk and Delhi Gate, the Ring Road between Shantivan Chowk and IP Flyover, Asaf Ali Road between Delhi Gate and Netaji Subhash Marg, Nishad Raj Marg from Shantivan Chowk, and Ranjit Singh Flyover from Guru Nanak Chowk. The Nagar Kirtan procession was scheduled to run from Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Chandni Chowk to Gurudwara Nanak Piao Sahib on GT Karnal Road, passing through a listed set of central Delhi locations including Fatehpuri, Khari Baoli, Naya Bazar Chowk, Peeli Kothi Road, Pul Mithai, Zorawar Singh Marg, Barf Khana Chowk, and Roshanara Road. The police noted that curbs along the procession route would depend on its movement, with impacts potentially extending to additional stretches such as Town Hall, Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Marg, Qutub Road Chowk, Pul Dufferin, Rani Jhansi Flyover, Sabzi Mandi, and Roop Nagar. The police urged commuters to plan journeys in advance, allow extra travel time, and avoid affected routes during the advisory periods.
items.title: Delhi Traffic Police Issue Advisories for Guru Nanak Jayanti VIP Movement and Nagar Kirtan on Monday

items.summary: Japanese material handling company Tadano has released the V320RC, a compact battery-electric wheeled pick-and-carry crane with a maximum lifting capacity of 35 tonnes. Developed in collaboration with NMG Italia and tested at that firm's job sites plus during setup operations at Marmomac in Verona, the machine is now available for purchase. The V320RC measures approximately 5 m long, 2.15 m wide, and 2.4 m tall, and runs on a 120V lithium-ion battery pack rated at 1,120 Ah (about 134 kWh). Its gross vehicle weight exceeds 31,150 kg (~34.5 short tons) and includes about 9,500 kg of removable counterweights to ease transport; a new hydraulic system pairs a variable-displacement pump with an electro-hydraulic control valve for precision and responsiveness while reducing energy use. NMG Italia reports the crane delivers roughly 50% better productivity than competing electric cranes under equivalent workloads, along with enough battery capacity for several days of operation between charges. The text notes that these performance claims are drawn from field testing by NMG Italia rather than independent verification.
items.title: Tadano launches 35-ton V320RC wheeled electric pick-and-carry crane

items.summary:
According to a statement from Myanmar's Defense Ministry published in state media, the country announced on Sunday that it has taken legal action against dozens of people—including local officials—accused of extortion and illegal detention of men attempting to avoid compulsory military service. The ministry framed this as an effort to combat graft within the conscription process, representing what appears to be a rare official acknowledgement of corruption in Myanmar's draft system.

The statement emerges amid ongoing conflict: the military is engaged against pro-democracy rebels and ethnic minority factions in a civil war that began with the 2021 coup which removed Aung San Suu Kyi's democratically elected government. The text notes this acknowledgment as significant given the context of the nation being described as 'war-torn.'

The source material is limited to an official statement and does not provide specific details on the number or identities of those charged, nor independent verification of the claims.
items.title: Myanmar Reports Legal Action Against Officials Over Military Draft Corruption

items.summary: Ahmed al Ahmed, a fruit seller born in Syria who moved to Australia in 2006, recounted his experience tackling one of the gunmen during the mass shooting at a Jewish festival on Bondi Beach. The incident occurred when he was visiting the Sydney beach with his cousin and heard shots fired into a crowd as gunfire continued around him; al Ahmed rushed forward to tackle one gunman while others kept firing. Writing nearly a year after what is described as Australia's worst mass shooting in decades, he said his wounds still ache and issued a plea for unity.
items.title: Bondi shooting hero reflects on wounds and calls for unity nearly a year later

items.summary:
At a media briefing in Delhi during his visit for the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) dialogue, Pakistan Minister Musadik Masood Malik declined to address questions on terrorism and the Indus Waters Treaty, stating he had not been invited by India for any bilateral talks. He said that without a formal mechanism or an explicit invitation from India, there is no basis for discussing bilateral issues, adding: "When you invite me for a discussion on those specific issues, I shall be there." Malik emphasized his visit was focused solely on the multilateral SCO meeting and not on bilateral engagement with India.

On terrorism, he said the matter could be addressed through evidence-based dialogue via bilateral or multilateral platforms, noting that both countries have suffered losses. He stated Pakistan has repeatedly offered to present its evidence in various forums, saying: "You bring your evidence, and we will bring ours." Regarding the Indus Waters Treaty, Malik repeated his position that he would discuss it only if India extended an invitation.

The report presents these statements as reported by the Pakistani minister; no independent verification of whether India issued any such invitations is provided in the text.
items.title: Pakistan minister declines bilateral questions, citing lack of Indian invitation

items.summary: Cricket Australia insists that its support for Pat Cummins to remain the Australian cricket captain is not an indication that it has chosen a side in the ongoing 'sandpaper' controversy. CA boss Todd Greenberg stated, "I am not putting someone's version of events over somebody else's," framing the backing as consistent with believing other players' accounts rather than dismissing them.
items.title: Cricket Australia says Cummins backing does not signal taking sides in sandpaper spat

items.summary: Australia's inaugural Recipe of the Year series concluded on its finale when Laura McLellan won the top prize for her Emerald Pie, a dish featuring green curry filling that references both her hometown in rural Queensland and its colour. The 36-year-old qualified nutritionist beat three home cook finalists—Jacqui Toumbas, Jimmy Stewart, and Ray Marouki—for the award after being judged by Country Women's Association judges Pia Miranda, Adam Liaw, and Ellice Schrader. McLellan grew up learning to cook from her mother, who immigrated with her father from Laos 40 years ago; she described winning as a surreal experience, noting she had not won an award since primary school. The three finalists praised the winner: Jimmy Stewart called McLellan's win deserved and likened the pie to humble pie on the outside with curry inside, Jacqui Toumbas described it as incredible and said many would recreate it at home, and Ray Marouki echoed that she had done an amazing job. The show was noted for its emphasis on accessible cooking using ingredients like frozen vegetables obtainable in regional areas, strong camaraderie among contestants, and the celebration of multiculturalism through diverse recipes.
items.title: Laura McLellan Wins ABC's Recipe of the Year with Emerald Pie

items.summary:
Toby Kiers, a biologist at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam and professor of Ecology and Evolution, became the youngest person to receive the 2026 Tyler Prize for Environmental Achievement. She was born in New York but raised in Connecticut before dropping out of college at 19; she later returned to study field biology after an internship that took her to a Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute station on an island in the Panama Canal, where she began studying mycorrhizal fungi—organisms associated with plant roots. Her research investigates how these brainless organisms make decisions and process information within underground networks.

Kiers reports that 90% of all plant species form connections with mycorrhizal fungi, and one study showed plants transfer roughly 13 billion tons of CO₂ annually to fungal networks—about one-third of fossil fuel emissions. She says the fungi use this carbon to build structures that hold soil together while supplying phosphorus and water to plants in deserts and arid zones.

She attributes much of the field's neglect to estimates that between two and three million fungal species exist on Earth with barely 1% identified, noting they are hard to see and short-lived. She describes threats including urban development, fungicides, agricultural intensification, and nitrogen from fertilizers in rainwater declining fungal diversity even in unmanaged forests.

In 2021 Kiers founded the Society for the Protection of Underground Networks (SPUN) to help secure international protections for underground fungi. SPUN created a subterranean atlas that identifies biodiversity hotspots using machine learning models fed by small grants awarded to scientists worldwide, and it maps uncertainty so predictions weaken with distance from actual samples. She reports 90% of hotspot locations fall outside currently protected areas—only about 10% have protection—and cites the Gobi Desert in Mongolia as an example of fungi surviving extreme conditions.

The article notes her team collaborates with AMOLF on imaging robots to track fungal development and decisions, and that one doctoral student studies whether flow patterns change over a day-night cycle. The text does not provide independent verification of Kiers's figures or the SPUN atlas statistics beyond what she states.
items.title: Toby Kiers Becomes Youngest Recipient of 2026 Tyler Prize for Research on Mycorrhizal Fungal Networks

items.summary: Netflix is streaming Gènesi, a six-episode Catalan-language series co-produced with 3Cat that chronicles Ferran Adrià's rise at El Bulli. The show premiered this fall; the chef describes it as potentially reaching a five-billion-person market while emphasizing its goal of relaunching what he calls the 'techno-emotional movement' in cooking, funded by the Generalitat to promote Catalonia and Spain. Adrià has accumulated 550 distinctions including three Michelin stars from 1997 until El Bulli closed in 2011, five-time best restaurant awards, six honorary doctorates (soon seven), a Chef of the Decade title, and recently the Gold Medal of Catalonia. The series dramatizes his career beginning when he joined as station chef in 1984 with no formal training, memorized El Practicón, then absorbed nouvelle cuisine from Jean-Paul Vinay's guidance on Bocuse and Guérard books; it also covers Joël Robuchon declaring Adrià the world's number one chef in 1996. Emotional arcs include Adrià's strained relationship with Santi Santamaría over molecular versus terroir cooking, his vow of silence during the 2008-2009 tabasco controversy involving then-prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, and Juli Soler's Alzheimer's before dying in 2015. Adrià argues El Bulli drove much global innovation—claiming 'in twenty years we did 80% of the world's innovation!'—and that Spain communicates its cuisine poorly because it lacked a name for their approach while northern Europe developed New Nordic Cuisine; he sees hope in the government's International Plan for Spanish Gastronomy. The series is explicitly not critical reassessment, features actor Miquel Fernández as Adrià, and recreates dishes matching pages from Catálogo General de El Bulli.
items.title: Ferran Adrià's Netflix Series 'Gènesi' Premieres as He Reflects on El Bulli and Spain's Culinary Standing

items.summary: South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday over an AI-assisted cheating scandal that emerged days before the Suneung university entrance exam. The crisis began last Sunday when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam admitted to using a miniature camera and smartphone to achieve a near-perfect score, just four days ahead of the nine-hour Suneung, which is widely regarded as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs, and better marriage prospects. In response, officials rolled out preventive measures such as blocking public Wi-Fi in testing areas and placing stickers over clothing buttons; however, Choi struggled to reassure the public, particularly after remarks he made three days before the exam. Writing on X, Choi stated that although the Suneung concluded without major incidents, he failed to prepare adequately in advance and accepted full responsibility for his resignation, which President Lee Jae Myung had already accepted. During a parliamentary hearing on Monday, when asked whether authorities could catch would-be cheaters on exam day, the 72-year-old replied that due to his age he was not confident they could—a response that drew public backlash. Choi did not appear at press conferences in the days leading up to Thursday's exam, where a vice minister instead announced preventive measures. Officials reported that 111 cases of misconduct involving electronic devices were identified during the exam, with nearly half detected through three emergency alerts sent by the government to identify smartphones test takers had failed to hand over.
items.title: South Korea's Education Minister Resigns Over AI-Assisted Exam Cheating Scandal

items.summary: The text presents NRDC's framing that increasing loss frequency and severity are outpacing insurers' ability to price and absorb them, which the organization attributes in part to climate change. This dynamic is said to drive higher premiums, reduced coverage availability, and insurer withdrawal from certain markets, thereby raising property ownership costs and exposing individuals, businesses, and communities to greater physical and financial risk. NRDC characterizes insurance as both a critical safety net for recovering from losses and a component of community resilience that supports faster recovery, continued investment, and adaptation when functioning effectively. The organization's director of insurance and financial risk, Alfonso Pating, is cited as explaining how homeowner's insurance works and why climate change makes it unaffordable. NRDC links associated reports on the insurability crisis to housing resilience and adaptation strategies.
items.title: NRDC Frames Rising Insurance Costs as a Climate-Driven Affordability Crisis

items.summary:
Tesla CEO Elon Musk denied affiliation with the MAGA movement during a New York Times DealBook Summit interview, though he did not apologize for his prior political support. CleanTechnica frames this denial as an early stage of what it calls a longer recovery process, arguing that accountability is approaching through Congress rather than spiritual means.

The article's central claim concerns SpaceX satellite services to Ukraine. According to the text, Musk took credit for providing "free" Starlink communications aid after Russia's 2014 invasion of Donbas and its 2022 assault on Kyiv failed militarily. CleanTechnica disputes this characterization with several figures: a later assessment attributed about 85% of initial terminal costs to other sources including USAID, while Poland and other groups contributed an estimated 30% of connectivity costs. The Belfer Center for International Affairs at Harvard concluded in 2023 that the U.S. government likely agreed to pay some or all ongoing operational costs.

The article states that SpaceX made unilateral decisions restricting Ukraine's use of the technology, with CEO Gwynne Shotwell asserting it was never intended "for offensive purposes." Musk reportedly further restricted service in October when he, Trump, or both reduced satellite support. In response, incoming House Intelligence Committee Chair Jim Himes (D-CT) sent a letter dated November 20 demanding an in-person briefing from senior SpaceX officers and warning that all present and future U.S. government contracts with SpaceX are at risk.

The text notes the Republican congressional majority is expected to end on January 3, when a Democratic majority takes over. It attributes ongoing service interruptions partly to Trump's engagement with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping during the same period. No charts or quantitative comparisons suitable for visualization were stated in the article.
items.title: Incoming Democratic Majority Threatens to Void SpaceX Contracts Over Starlink Service Disruptions in Ukraine

items.summary:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the Trump administration is seeking answers from Nvidia about its chip sales to China and wants to determine who held responsibility for compliance following chief executive Jensen Huang's resignation. According to Bessent, the administration has contacted Nvidia's interim management, board members, and legal team but had not yet received responses regarding the company's compliance practices or how widely awareness of reported issues extended through its ranks; he emphasized that it 'behooves Nvidia to move quickly' so officials can assess whether knowledge reached lower levels, middle management, or leadership. Bessent expressed confidence that the board would conduct a thorough review and noted his earlier recommendation on Fox News that Nvidia seek a new chief executive outside the company given concerns about internal culture, while urging its board and external legal advisers to address compliance questions within 10 days.

The administration's pressure follows Huang's resignation amid reports of alleged relationships, including an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Megaspeed International—an Nvidia customer—whom US intelligence reportedly suspects was involved in espionage for China. These allegations triggered investigations by US regulators and the FBI, congressional action, an internal company review, and a proposed investor class-action lawsuit.

On policy grounds, Trump said on Friday he would like Huang to apologize and return to Nvidia; Bessent declined to take a position pending more information. Separately, days after Huang's resignation the administration issued new export controls further restricting China's access to advanced AI chips from companies such as Nvidia, tightening restrictions ahead of Trump's visit with President Xi Jinping.

On corporate governance, Nvidia board chairman Harvey Jones said the company would not rehire Huang, and on November 10 its independent board members appointed Wall Street law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an independent investigation following reports by The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal. All of these developments are drawn from statements attributed to Bessent, Trump, Harvey Jones, and reporting cited in the article; no verification beyond those sources is provided.
items.title: Trump Administration Presses Nvidia for Answers on China Chip Sales Amid Jensen Huang Fallout

items.summary: Amid rising energy demand from the AI era, Google signed a power purchase agreement with Quaise Energy for **50 megawatts** of superhot geothermal power to be produced in Central Oregon at Project Obsidian. The deal signals commercial progress for enhanced geothermal technology, which taps Earth's heat by drilling deep enough that it becomes viable nearly anywhere rather than only where natural thermal vents exist on the surface. Quaise relies on MIT-developed vacuum-tube gyrotron technology that sends high-frequency electromagnetic waves down a borehole to vaporize rock molecules while a gas jet clears ash, and Project Obsidian aims to begin delivering energy as soon as 2030. The article notes significant limitations: enhanced geothermal remains in its infancy with high up-front and operational costs due to lack of scale, represents just **0.4 percent** of the U.S. energy mix despite the country's roughly **3.7 gigawatts** of installed capacity leading globally, and is not yet commercially scalable. The piece cites a Rhodium Group report estimating geothermal could meet up to **64 percent** of data center energy demand growth by the early 2030s.
items.title: Google Signs 50 MW Superhot Geothermal Purchase Agreement With Quaise Energy at Project Obsidian

items.summary: At least three bodies have been recovered from the site of a residential building hit by a Russian strike in Ukraine's Kyiv region, according to the country's State Emergency Services. A woman in her forties and a teenage boy have so far been identified among those killed as rescue workers continue searching the rubble for survivors; some people were evacuated earlier that day. Rescue efforts are being hampered by continued warnings of drone threats near the site. Reporting from Kyiv region, BBC's Sarah Rainsford quoted one woman describing the situation as 'living a nightmare,' reflecting residents' perception that danger is escalating.
items.title: Ukrainians Search Rubble After Russian Strike on Residential Building in Kyiv Region

items.summary: Laura Gallacher, the wife of convicted sex offender Russell Brand, promised in a Sunday episode of their Christian series 'Sunday Service' that she would 'absolutely honour' the rules set by HMP Littlehey where her husband is held. The statement came after Andy Burnham called on Google to remove a video from Brand's YouTube channel containing his message protesting his innocence while serving a 10-and-a-half-year sentence for rape and sexual assaults, following convictions at Southwark crown court on 5 November. Gallacher said she would continue the series because 'I really enjoy it' and framed her role as defending her family amid media scrutiny of whether she is an appropriate figure to run his channel during a Ministry of Justice inquiry into whether Brand breached rules designed to prevent serious distress to victims. The disputed video, titled 'The Good Work Continues,' has accumulated more than 1m views since its publication last Sunday and remains online despite repeated requests from ministers for removal; it became the best-performing video on his channel since a December conversation with influencer Candace Owens, contrasting with many of his other recent videos drawing only between 50,000 and 100,000 views. Burnham noted he 'wouldn't leap' to change the law but urged social media companies to take down such content, arguing victims should not have to hear from Brand.
items.title: Russell Brand's wife vows to follow prison rules amid YouTube video controversy

items.summary:
Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told CNN's 'State of the Union' on November 22 that Americans should expect additional technology outages and disruptions as companies and government agencies replace aging systems. He stated, "And as part of that ongoing upgrade, we are going to have glitches, gaps, interruptions in service... That is going to happen." Clayton framed these upgrades as necessary to improve performance and cybersecurity amid technological advances straining older infrastructure.

His comments followed a string of technology failures this month that disrupted critical US systems, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft email outage, technical glitches affecting several major banks, and a temporary disruption to the National Security Agency's network. Clayton attributed these outages to technical upgrades rather than coordinated or state-sponsored actions, reiterating his previous statements on ABC's 'This Week.'

The report notes that Clayton declined to discuss specifics of separate reports regarding cyberattacks on the FBI and Department of Agriculture, saying he expects investigators to provide answers "in due course." The text presents these claims as attributed to Clayton without independent verification.
items.title: US Intelligence Chief Predicts More Tech Outages Amid System Upgrades

items.summary: A man based in Chandigarh posted on Reddit that he earned approximately **₹39,000** during his first month as a delivery partner for the quick-commerce platform Blinkit. He attributed the income to long shifts—about 12 hours on weekdays and nearly 16 hours over weekends when customer orders surged—and said tips from customers added to his earnings. The post is grounded solely in this single viral social media contribution; LiveMint explicitly states it cannot independently verify the content's authenticity and does not endorse it, so the figures should be treated as an unverified personal account rather than confirmed data.
items.title: Chandigarh delivery partner reports ₹39,000 first-month earnings on Blinkit

items.summary:
During an interview on NBC's Meet the Press, Louisiana Republican Senator John Kennedy invoked Greek mythology to describe former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's reported affair with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang (Huang Le), calling it "the most expensive sex since Helen of Troy." The remark came in response to host Kristen Welker's question about whether national security was at risk given Nvidia's central role in the AI boom. Huang stepped down as CEO on 12 November following allegations involving extramarital relationships with Alice Huang and two Nvidia employees.

The reported affair connects to broader export-control concerns: Megaspeed International, where Alice Huang served as executive director, facilitated approximately $12 billion in chip sales that allegedly violated US restrictions prohibiting advanced AI chips from China. National intelligence director Jay Clayton stated on CNN's State of the Union that he suspected China obtained Nvidia's most advanced AI chips and told Fox News Sunday that "there are chips that have ended up in places that they should not." Kennedy said his focus was less on Huang's personal conduct than on how China circumvented export controls, directing questions toward Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

The article notes that Lutnick faced scrutiny for allegedly ignoring warnings about Megaspeed smuggling chips to China, while other administration officials reportedly wanted to blacklist the company but commerce department stalled enforcement. Kennedy characterized commerce leaders as either incompetent or knowingly complicit and called for them to testify under oath before a Senate committee. Bessent told CBS News's Face the Nation that the Trump administration had contacted Nvidia's temporary management and lawyers to determine who oversaw compliance, stating it "behooves Nvidia to move quickly on this." The piece also observes that Kennedy is known for his colloquialisms and southern drawl despite holding degrees from Vanderbilt University, the University of Virginia School of Law, and Oxford University.
items.title: Louisiana Senator John Kennedy Characterizes Jensen Huang's Alleged Affair as 'Most Expensive Sex Since Helen of Troy'

items.summary:
A CNBC report profiles Charles Broomfield, a 26-year-old Google employee and YouTuber who is on track to earn about $323,000 (approximately ₹3 crore) in 2026. Despite the high income, his annual living expenses remain below $20,000 (₹18.56 lakh), which CNBC notes is less than what a full-time US minimum-wage worker would earn across all 50 states at an estimated $23,700 annually. His core monthly spending in August totaled about $1,477 while he invested another $17,931 into his 401(k) and brokerage account; the breakdown included roughly $1,098 for rent and utilities (shared with four roommates), $229 for a kickboxing gym membership, $48 on Uber, about $28 on food after eating most meals at work, $15 in insurance, $59 discretionary spending, and $700 toward an employer tuition repayment plan. Sharing the apartment reportedly saves him around $1,000 monthly versus renting alone, while Google covers his Metro commute and he relies on walking, cycling, and public transit instead of owning a car.

The report attributes these habits to childhood financial training—his parents encouraged saving half of earnings—and to Broomfield's exposure at 17 to the FIRE movement via Mr. Money Mustache. After graduating from Knox College in 2022 with an early job paying more than $100,000 annually, he set a goal of accumulating $750,000 before turning 30; CNBC reports he has already built roughly $650,000 since graduation and expects to reach the target within about a year. Extreme measures are described as part of his approach, including considering living in a van parked at Google's garage and cycling two miles once to save approximately $1 on toothpaste.

The article frames this behavior primarily as a means to financial independence rather than early retirement or luxury consumption; Broomfield says he does not necessarily want to stop working and hopes instead to build an AI security business. The ultimate goal, per the report, is freedom from income anxiety—knowing he could survive losing his job tomorrow. No explicit savings percentage figure was provided in the text despite the headline's "nearly 90%" claim.

The figures are described as approximate and rounded using a stated exchange rate of US$1 = ₹93; CNBC characterizes Broomfield's $20,000 spending level as an estimate for recent years rather than a precisely verified figure. The report also notes his plans to build a business are aspirational intentions attributed to him via the outlet rather than confirmed outcomes.
items.title: Google AI security analyst Charles Broomfield saves nearly 90% of a $323,000 income while targeting financial independence before age 30

items.summary: NVIDIA released Alpamayo 2 Edge, a compact reasoning vision-language-action (VLA) model designed to run inside vehicles on NVIDIA DRIVE AGX Thor rather than in datacenter GPUs. The model is marketed as approximately 2B parameters—comprising a 2.45B backbone paired with a 0.2B diffusion action expert—though Hugging Face metadata lists it at 3B; its context length was not disclosed but measured prompt reached about 3,236 tokens. It converts surround-camera video into plans spanning up to 6.4 seconds and is the in-car counterpart of the larger Alpamayo 2 Super cloud model (about 34B). The architecture draws on NVIDIA Cosmos 3 Edge with a Nemotron-based backbone and includes a SigLIP2 encoder, reading inputs from six cameras across 22 frames plus navigation instructions and 20 historical ego poses to output 64 waypoints. Training combined offline distillation from Alpamayo 2 Super-generated Chain-of-Causation autolabels using roughly 115,000 hours of multi-camera driving video and about 3.7 million traces, followed by closed-loop reinforcement learning in AlpaGym. Performance highlights include approximately 15.15 km per at-fault incident in the AlpaSim simulation (about 60 times Qwen-Drive-1.0's 4B model), with open-loop minADE of about 0.52 to 0.53 meters; however, it trails Alpamayo 2 Super and Qwen-Drive on LingoQA at a score of 75.2 versus the cloud model's 79.2. Latency figures range from 160 ms to 190 ms for pixel-to-trajectory planning under an FP8 TensorRT recipe, though PyTorch BF16 inference runs much slower at about 0.76 Hz in NVIDIA's demo video and the optimized pipeline reaches roughly 13 Hz in simulation; real-time performance on Thor requires this FP8 optimization rather than raw PyTorch execution. Validation is limited to a single H100 (measuring about 12.06 GiB peak memory) for workstation reference, with other GPU architectures unvalidated and context length undisclosed. The release also included AlpaJudge, an RL reward that reportedly improved reasoning quality by roughly 10% to 11%, distributed under the OpenMDW-1.1 license with Apache 2.0 code.
items.title: NVIDIA Releases Alpamayo 2 Edge: A Compact Reasoning VLA for Autonomous Driving

items.summary: In response to Sim Eng Cheong's October 19 letter proposing that ActiveSG replenish members' credits to $100 annually, Sport Singapore chief Tan Hock Leong declined the specific suggestion while outlining existing measures designed to keep Singaporeans active. Rather than adopting automatic annual top-ups, SportSG describes a broader approach centered on affordable facility access, varied programmes for different needs, and incentives for healthy behaviours. ActiveSG gym entry fees are set at $2.50 for adults (with lower concession rates for students and seniors), while swimming pool entry is $1 for adults; members aged above 65 receive free access to all gyms and pools. New members receive an initial $100 in credits, and existing members may carry forward unused credits provided they make at least one transaction each year. Additionally, since September 2026, Health Promotion Board Healthpoints can be converted into ActiveSG credits, offering another pathway to earn credits through healthy behaviours. Tan Hock Leong noted that SportSG will continue reviewing its facilities, programmes, and support measures to help Singaporeans integrate sport and physical activity into everyday life.
items.title: ActiveSG Chief Responds to Proposal for Annual $100 Credit Top-Ups

items.summary: In a forum response following Brazil's 7-0 victory over Singapore, writer A. Thiyaga Raju argues that rare fixtures against elite opposition should be deliberately used to develop young players rather than being judged solely by the scoreline. While acknowledging the value of experienced players like Hariss Harun and goalkeeper Izwan Mahbud, he contends that even 20 to 30 minutes against Brazil's world-class squad could provide valuable lessons in speed, movement, positioning, decision-making, and composure under pressure—experiences difficult to replicate domestically. He frames such friendlies as platforms for nurturing emerging talent 'carefully, deliberately and with the future in mind,' while noting he is not advocating fielding an entirely inexperienced team or disregarding experience. The piece presents these views as opinion rather than established fact; no concrete data on player development outcomes was provided.
items.title: Singapore Football Forum: Using Marquee Friendlies to Expose Young Players

items.summary: The Indian Navy has relaxed its rules so that Naval Agniveers who choose the two-year 'Second Tour of Duty' after their initial four-year stint may marry, though only after completing mandatory professional and trade-specific training. A defence source told TOI that such personnel can then take leave for marriage purposes; the provision does not currently apply to Agniveers aged 17.5 to 21 during the initial service period under the Agnipath scheme. The relaxation arrives as the first batch, recruited in late 2022, finishes its four-year term this month and follows the Union Cabinet's approval of an extended-service option. On Nov 4, Chief of Defence Staff General N S Raja Subramani announced the 'Second Tour of Duty,' extending Agniveers' service from four to six years with higher pay; continued personnel may also be enrolled as regular soldiers if they meet selection criteria and wish to stay on. Extended-tenure Agniveers are set to receive Rs 43,500 per month in the first year of extension and Rs 47,500 per month in the second year (plus allowances), with the government's Seva Nidhi contribution rising to 70% during those two years. The source noted that the Indian Army and Air Force could subsequently adopt similar marriage provisions under their own specifications.
items.title: Indian Navy permits marriage for Agniveers opting into a two-year service extension

items.summary: Ladakh chief secretary Ashish Kundra on Sunday welcomed the voter turnout in Saturday's elections, which he said reflected public demand for democracy as he appealed for participation in LAHDC (hill council) voting scheduled for Dec 4. Turnout was reported at **70.03%** in panchayat polls and **52.4%** in municipal polls; Kundra noted these were the first elections held since Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019, following the previous round in 2018. He said autonomy talks between Ladakhi representatives and the Union home ministry would resume after the LAHDC election, though he asked climate activist Sonam Wangchuk not to make provocative statements during the campaign. Kundra disputed LAB's claim that about **40%** of residents were absent from the region, stating only 10 to 12 days remained before voting and asserting that a majority had already cast ballots. He also urged Ladakhi representatives not to outright reject proposals offered by the Centre under Article 371 during MHA talks.
items.title: Ladakh chief secretary cites high panchayat turnout ahead of December 4 hill council polls

items.summary: Australian officials conceded that nations at this year's UN climate summit failed to reach an agreement, with social services minister Tanya Plibersek calling the outcome 'frustrating' and environment minister Chris Bowen describing the negotiated red lines as 'unbridgeable.' The deal fell short partly because it omitted the word 'fossil fuels,' a compromise that satisfied neither fossil fuel producers nor climate-affected nations. Deputy Liberal leader Jane Hume criticized Labor for co-hosting the summit, which ran overtime to become the longest COP ever and cost approximately $150m, while walking away without an agreement—the first since Kevin Rudd's 2009 Copenhagen failure—though Bowen defended his leadership by stating 'Australia left nothing on the field.' Concurrently, a Newspoll published in The Australian showed Labor leader Anthony Albanese trailing Coalition counterpart Angus Taylor as preferred prime minister for the first time, with Albanese's net approval rating hitting a new low of minus 31 and the Coalition's primary vote at 22% behind One Nation and Labor tied at 27%. Separately, the Lowy Institute's Asia Power Index reported that US foreign policy influence fell to its sharpest decline in nine years across eight criteria. In domestic legislative matters, communications minister Anika Wells announced a small-business carveout for digital duty of care legislation before it takes effect 12 months later, addressing business concerns about penalties exceeding $100m while the Greens continue negotiations over tougher penalties and an ombudsman.
items.title: Australia Walks Away From COP Without a Climate Deal as Albanese Trails in Newspoll

items.summary:
The Democratic Party won its largest majority in the US House of Representatives since 1992, driven by Democrat Chuck Hubbard unseating Republican Representative Virginia Foxx in North Carolina's Fifth Congressional District. The race was called Sunday after a recount requested under state law because the margin fell below 1%, with Hubbard beating Foxx by **330 votes** at **99%** of ballots counted. In aggregate, Democrats hold at least **258 House seats**, matching the total Republicans held in 1992 when Bill Clinton won the presidency and Democrats captured **258 seats**; Republicans now hold at least **173 seats**. Hubbard had lost to Foxx by nine percentage points in the 2024 midterms, but this result followed a series of Democratic upsets in deeply Republican districts across South Carolina, Texas, Alaska, and Iowa. Campaign messaging centered on rising living costs amid what candidates described as an Iran war, with President Trump and Vice President JD Vance suggesting inflation tied to that conflict contributed to the losses. Hubbard pledged to prioritize working families and small businesses while supporting public education and expanding affordable healthcare.

The party also controls the Senate alongside its House majority, giving it leverage to investigate conflicts of interest involving the president and his allies, confirm or block cabinet and judicial nominations, and advance legislation—though Trump retains veto power over enacted bills. Remaining uncalled races include Tennessee's fourth district, where Democrat Victoria Broderick leads by fewer than **300 votes**, and Minnesota's first district, where Democrat Jake Johnson is ahead by fewer than **500 votes**; two Louisiana elections will proceed to a December runoff.
items.title: Democrats Secure Largest House Majority Since 1992 After Flipping North Carolina's Fifth District

items.summary: An analysis by Transparency International Australia found that bosses at ten datacentre companies secured almost 120 meetings—specifically 119—with premiers or ministers across New South Wales, Victoria, Tasmania, Queensland, and the ACT over a three-year period. These are the only jurisdictions to publicly release ministerial diaries, so the count reflects just those five states rather than all of Australia's decision-makers. The report argues that when combined with political donations, this access demonstrates 'unfettered' influence creating an uneven playing field for other industries.
items.title: Transparency International Australia analysis finds datacentre executives held nearly 120 meetings with state premiers and ministers over three years

items.summary: The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey, concluded without an agreement after countries failed to reach consensus on a new deal. Negotiations broke down two days past their scheduled end date, making them the longest-running talks in the summit's history. The EU and other nations rejected a fourth draft agreement because it did not include language calling for a phase-out of fossil fuels, which they identify as the largest driver of global climate change. An EU representative accused some oil-producing states of hijacking the negotiations, while Russia defended its opposition to such a commitment in remarks that included direct criticism of the EU. The report is attributed to BBC climate and science reporter Esme Stallard.
items.title: COP31 Climate Talks End Without a Deal After Fossil Fuel Language Dispute

items.summary:
The United Nations' COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey, ended Sunday afternoon without consensus on its cover decision—the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity—marking the first such failure since 2009. The talks, attended by more than 100,000 participants and run two days beyond their scheduled end under Conference of the Parties president Murat Kurum of Turkey and negotiation leader Chris Bowen of Australia, still adopted several decisions, including a program to help workers transition away from fossil fuels and a plan to assess progress on climate adaptation. The deadlock stemmed primarily from deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much financing developed countries should provide to developing nations affected by climate disasters. A central aim of the meeting was to set quantifiable but voluntary global goals for economic electrification and increase funding for developing-country adaptation; these were not achieved in a unified statement.

The proposed text faced formal rejection from major blocs, including the European Union's 28-member group under Ireland's rotating presidency, several Latin American countries, and Pacific Island states. EU climate minister Darragh O'Brien stated his delegation objected because the decision omitted any mention of fossil fuels, which he called "the key driver of climate change." In contrast, Mohammad Ayoub of Saudi Arabia's energy ministry defended carbon dioxide removal and carbon capture technologies as necessary solutions to keep 1.5 degrees Celsius within reach—the long-term goal set by the 2015 Paris agreement—and noted that his country's 22-member League of Arab States supported the Antalya Pact.

The outcome reflects a broader decline in international climate collaboration since earlier agreements, including Egypt's 2022 establishment of a loss and damage fund and Dubai's 2023 adoption of language calling for a "just and orderly" fossil fuel transition by more than 190 countries. Climate envoy Kathy Jetn̄il-Kijiner of the Marshall Islands rejected the deal as undermining her country's security, while UN Secretary-General António Guterres expressed disappointment but insisted that "this setback does not change the facts," reaffirming that fossil fuels remain driving the crisis. The article frames this outcome as a serious but non-fatal setback to global climate efforts; it notes no quantifiable targets were adopted and attributes specific objections and positions directly to named officials, while omitting any independent verification of claims about future impacts or the scientific validity of carbon capture. No chart data is provided in the source text.
items.title: UN COP31 Climate Conference Ends Without Consensus on Cover Decision

items.summary: On Sunday, Nov. 22, Carlos Alcaraz defeated world number one Alexander Zverev **6**-**7**(**) on his way to winning the ATP Finals in Turin, securing his first title at the event after finishing as runner-up the previous year. The match score was reported as 6-2, 7-6(7). Alcaraz saved three set points before closing out a comeback victory that extended his streak to **14** consecutive wins and marked his third straight title of the season, having also won in Vienna and Paris. At **23**, he became the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam while capturing what had been described as the biggest tour title eluding him. Since losing in the US Open quarter-finals, Alcaraz posted a **22**-**1** record across four titles. Zverev's loss ended his most successful season, during which he won his first two Grand Slam titles and rose to the top of the world rankings; as a two-time ATP Finals champion, this defeat marked an end to that run. Alcaraz had returned from a **four**-month break due to a wrist injury before the event. In the match itself, Zverev struggled with his serve and committed **19** unforced errors in the first set alone, dropping early breaks as Alcaraz took control; by the fifth game of that set he had accumulated **15** unforced errors after earning five break points against him during his first two service games. Zverev later recovered one break to narrow the deficit to **4**-**2**, but a subsequent time-violation dispute with the umpire preceded another Alcaraz break and eventual tiebreak, which he won despite failing to convert any of three consecutive set points.
items.title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev to claim maiden ATP Finals title in Turin
